rows.title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Model for Predicting Molecular Subtypes of Human Breast Cancer Using Multimodal Data
rows.authors: T. Liu, J. Huang, T. Liao, R. Pu, S. Liu, Y. Peng (OpenAlex expands these to Tao Liu, Junhao Huang, Tianchi Liao, Ruitao Pu, ShengZheng Liu, Yue Peng). The Unpaywall author record gives the corresponding author as T. Liu, College of Information Engineering, Sichuan Agricultural University, Yaan, China.
rows.venue: IRBM (Elsevier), vol. 43, issue 1, pp. 62-74. Refereed journal. Bibliographic data verified by me against the Crossref API (HTTP 200): container-title IRBM, volume 43, issue 1, page 62-74, published-print [[2022,2]], published-online None. DATE AMBIGUITY, recorded rather than resolved: Semantic Scholar indexes the year as 2021, Unpaywall returns published_date 2021-01-10 (the online-first date) and year 2021, and the DOI stem is 2020. All three were seen; this row uses the Crossref published-print year.
rows.modalities: PER THE PUBLISHER ABSTRACT, which is the only primary text reachable for this paper: 'We combine the patient's gene modality data with image modality data to construct a multimodal fusion framework.' The abstract names exactly two modalities, 'gene modality' and 'image modality'. It NEVER says copy number, never says CNV, never says gene expression, and never says whole-slide image; those five strings were confirmed absent from the complete abstract text. Whether the image modality is histopathology at all is not established by any text opened for this row. SECONDARY ATTRIBUTION ONLY, never a reading of Liu et al.: Amer et al. arXiv:2509.03408, related-work section, verbatim - 'Liu et al. (2022b) integrate CNV, gene expression, and WSI data from TCGA-BRCA for PAM50 breast cancer subtyping. Their approach employs PCA for genomic feature reduction, VGG16 for WSI feature extraction, and weighted averaging optimized via simulated annealing for final predictions.' Amer's reference-list entry confirms it is this paper (Irbm, 43(1):62-74, 2022b). The entire WSI+CNV characterisation of this paper rests on that one secondary sentence.
rows.datasets: TCGA-BRCA. Abstract verbatim: 'We used the TCGA-BRCA dataset as a sample set for molecular subtype prediction of breast cancer. It is a public dataset that can be obtained through the following link: https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/projects/TCGA-BRCA'. NO cohort n appears anywhere in the abstract. A figure of roughly 831 usable cases of 1098 circulates in secondary sources (Borji et al. 2026 Table 3 attributes '~831 usable samples after filtering from 1098 patients' to this paper) but it was NOT confirmed against anything primary; recorded as NR.
rows.endpoint: 'molecular subtype prediction of breast cancer' / 'predicting breast cancer subtypes', abstract verbatim. The string PAM50 does not appear in the publisher abstract; PAM50 is attributed to this paper only by Amer et al. arXiv:2509.03408 (secondary). CLASS COUNT: NR - the abstract never enumerates the classes, never gives an output-layer dimension and never says four or five, and no secondary source opened for this row states a class count either. PREDICTION UNIT: NR - the abstract says 'the patient's gene modality data with image modality data', which implies a patient-keyed record, but never states whether prediction and scoring are per patient, per case or per slide/image; given how sensitive this literature is to that choice, treat it as a material gap rather than a footnote. LABEL BASIS: NR from the primary source, which says only 'molecular subtype'; RNA-derived PAM50 is attributed by Amer (secondary) and the caller (nearest-centroid, genefu, Netanely or nCounter) is unstated by both.
rows.wsi_pipeline: NR from the primary source. The abstract says only: 'According to the different forms and states, we set up feature extraction networks respectively'; 'we use the principal component analysis to reduce the dimensionality of high-dimensional data of gene modality and filter the data of image modality'; and 'we also improve the traditional feature extraction network to make it show better performance.' No tile size, magnification, encoder, MIL aggregator or bag construction is stated anywhere in the abstract. SECONDARY ONLY: Amer et al. say VGG16 was used for WSI feature extraction.
rows.fusion_method: LATE, described as a weighted linear aggregation. Abstract verbatim: 'we fuse the output of the two feature networks based on the idea of weighted linear aggregation. Finally, the fused features are used to predict breast cancer subtypes.' The abstract's own wording ('the fused features') points at FEATURE-level rather than probability-level combination, which would make it NOT an antecedent of an equal-weight probability mean. How the weights were optimised is NR in the abstract; simulated annealing is attested only by Amer (secondary). NO equal-weight-mean baseline is mentioned anywhere in the abstract.
rows.metrics: ALL FROM THE PUBLISHER ABSTRACT; the body and every table are unreachable (see caveats). Re-retrieved and confirmed verbatim from the Semantic Scholar Graph API record for DOI:10.1016/j.irbm.2020.12.002 (HTTP 200), which carries the full structured Elsevier abstract, and independently corroborated by the OpenAIRE record. VERBATIM: 'Our model achieved a prediction accuracy of 88.07% in 10 times of 10-fold cross-validation.' -> metric = prediction accuracy; split type = 10 times of 10-fold cross-validation; aggregation unit NR. VERBATIM: 'We did a separate AUC test for each subtype, and the average AUC value obtained was 0.9427.' -> metric = the mean of per-subtype AUCs, i.e. an unweighted average of one-vs-rest AUCs, although the abstract never uses the words macro or one-vs-rest; SPLIT TYPE IS NOT RESTATED for this number and it is not explicitly tied to the 10x10-fold protocol. VERBATIM: 'In terms of subtype prediction accuracy, our model is about 7.45% higher than the previous average.' No per-modality unimodal number, no confidence interval, no per-class number and no balanced accuracy appears in the abstract. UNVERIFIED against the body for internal consistency: neither 88.07% nor 0.9427 could be checked against a methods section, because ScienceDirect returns HTTP 403.
rows.external_validation: NONE STATED. Only TCGA-BRCA is named as a data source and the only protocol named is 10 times of 10-fold cross-validation. Absence cannot be positively established from an abstract, so the honest form is: no external cohort is mentioned in any text that could be opened for this row.
rows.code: NR - no repository is mentioned in the abstract, and the body is unreachable.
rows.caveats: PAYWALL, FULLY BLOCKING, AND THE REASON THIS ROW IS ABSTRACT-ONLY. Publisher Elsevier / ScienceDirect. Observed in this session: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1959031820301858 returns HTTP 403 Forbidden; curl -L on the DOI returns HTTP 200 but terminates at linkinghub.elsevier.com, which is the redirect shell and not the article; api.unpaywall.org/v2/10.1016/j.irbm.2020.12.002 returns is_oa false, oa_status 'closed', has_repository_copy false and oa_locations [] , so no legitimate open copy exists anywhere; a paper-search sweep across crossref, openalex, semantic, core, base, openaire, citeseerx and zenodo surfaced the record but no full text. THEREFORE UNVERIFIED, and permanently so unless someone buys the article: the class count; whether copy number is an input at all; the CNV granularity and any PCA reduction applied to it; whether the image modality is WSI; the cohort n and inclusion filter; whether the aggregated quantity is probabilities or features; how the weights were optimised; whether an equal-weight baseline was reported; the aggregation unit of the two headline metrics; the unimodal arms; and the existence of an external cohort. Refereed (Elsevier journal). THE PREMISE THAT THIS PAPER REFUTES 'Amer 2025 is the only WSI+CNV PAM50 work' IS NOT ESTABLISHED by anything readable - it survives only on Amer's own one-sentence characterisation of it, and other papers in this batch (CustOmics P52, MRSVM P60) refute that claim on full-text evidence instead. A FURTHER TRAP: if gene EXPRESSION really is one of its modalities and the labels really are PAM50, both as Amer says, then under this project's own leakage rule the 0.9427 is target-leaking exactly as CustOmics is, and the paper is not a clean WSI+CNV antecedent in any case. HOW TO USE IT: context only, and it cannot be promoted without the paywalled text. It is the closest published antecedent in FORM to an equal-weight probability mean - a weighted linear aggregation of two per-modality branches on TCGA-BRCA subtypes - so it bears on the positioning claim that nobody reports the trivial average; but its own abstract says 'the fused features are used to predict', which points at feature-level rather than probability-level combination, and it reports NO equal-weight baseline, so it does not pre-empt that result either way. It is NOT a comparator to any AUROC in this project: 0.9427 is an average of per-subtype AUCs on internal TCGA 10x10-fold CV with the aggregation unit unknown, against a case-level pooled out-of-fold macro AUROC internally and a case-level external CPTAC figure.

rows.title: Multimodal CustOmics: A unified and interpretable multi-task deep learning framework for multimodal integrative data analysis in oncology
rows.authors: Hakim Benkirane, Maria Vakalopoulou, David Planchard, Julien Adam, Ken Olaussen, Stefan Michiels, Paul-Henry Cournede
rows.venue: PLOS Computational Biology 21(6):e1013012, published 17 June 2025 (received 30 July 2024, accepted 31 March 2025). Refereed, open access, peer-review history published. Front matter confirmed independently via Europe PMC (PMID 40526743); the DOI resolves HTTP 200 to journals.plos.org.
rows.modalities: H&E whole-slide images plus multi-omics. Methods verbatim: 'The new version of our multimodal network can jointly integrate H&E slides and molecular profile features (mutation status, copy-number variation, RNA sequencing [RNA-seq] expression, DNA methylation, etc.).' For the reported experiments the three omics types are RNA-seq, CNV and methylation (S3 Table enumerates exactly CNV / RNAseq / Methyl and their pairwise and triple combinations). CONFIRMED on full text: this IS a WSI+CNV paper and it IS a PAM50 paper - but on the BRCA endpoint the CNV never appears without RNA-seq, which is the whole story of the row.
rows.datasets: TCGA pan-cancer from the GDC, 'comprising 11,768 patients across 33 tumor types'. Eight cohorts are used for survival; 'Three of these eight cohorts were also utilized to assess classification into molecular subtypes: TCGA-BRCA, TCGA-COAD, and TCGA-STAD.' The private validation cohort is IALT (International Adjuvant Lung Cancer Trial), NSCLC, used only for survival interpretability. The BRCA task n is NOT stated in the main text. S1 Table (XLSX, downloaded from the PLOS supplementary endpoint .s001, HTTP 200, and parsed cell by cell from xl/worksheets/sheet1.xml) gives the TCGA-BRCA row as Mutations 1082, CNV 1082, RNAseq 1179, Methylation 881, WSI 1133, Overall 1283 (6.8%). The effective n for the PAM50 subtype task, i.e. the intersection with a PAM50 label, is NR.
rows.endpoint: Molecular subtype classification on TCGA-BRCA, explicitly PAM50: 'Fig 2 presents interpretability findings concerning the PAM50 subtype classification within the TCGA-BRCA dataset', with the Fig 2 caption titled 'PAM50 interpretability analysis'. Also survival (C-index) on eight cohorts and pan-cancer tumour-type classification. NOTE ON HOW THIN THAT LINK IS: the string PAM50 occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the whole body, in that Section 4.2 sentence; the Table 1 caption and the Datasets section say only 'molecular subtypes', so the PAM50 identity of the Table 1 BRCA column is established indirectly rather than stated at the table. CLASS COUNT: NR, established by exhaustive negative check - the paper never enumerates the PAM50 classes, never says four or five, never gives an output dimension, and grepping the complete full text for Basal / LumA / Luminal / Normal-like returns zero hits; the only class name appearing anywhere is 'Her2 subtype' in the Fig 2 interpretability discussion. Whether Normal-like is included is therefore unknown, which matters because it is the single biggest driver of apparent PAM50 difficulty. PREDICTION UNIT: case/patient, established from the architecture ('The resulting patient-level representation z_moe_i is then passed through a final linear layer, mapping it to the model's final prediction') and from S1 Table, which counts 'the number of patients available for each modality'. LABEL BASIS: RNA-derived PAM50; the caller is NR, the paper naming the label only as 'PAM50 subtype classification within the TCGA-BRCA dataset' with no assignment method or source table.
rows.wsi_pipeline: Hypergraph encoding of WSI patches - a multiple-instance variational autoencoder with modality dropout, in which patches are re-encoded by a hypergraph encoder rather than a transformer. S4 Table ablates hypergraph against a visual transformer and S7 Table compares learnable parameter counts. Tile size, magnification, patch encoder and bag size are NR in the article text.
rows.fusion_method: Mixed-integration variational autoencoder producing a mixture-of-experts representation, with hierarchical MoE fusion over pathway-level and patient-level experts, plus modality dropout for robustness to missing modalities. Multiphase training, verbatim: 'During the first phase, we train each modality independently to obtain unsupervised sub-representations for the different bags. The second phase consists of unfreezing the central encoding network that learns the supervised representation of the final omics bag.' A trained joint operator throughout; there is NO untrained probability-mean baseline anywhere in the paper.
rows.metrics: Table 1, caption verbatim: 'Table 1. Classification performances. Comparison of the classification performances for the 4 tasks concerning the area under ROC (AUC %) +/- the standard deviation across the folds.' Split type verbatim: 'The input dataset was randomly split into training, validation, and testing sets (60-20-20%) using stratified 5-fold cross-validation'. All values below are the BRCA column, AUC %, internal 5-fold CV on TCGA, patient level. Multi-Omics block: SNN 92.0 +/- 3.3; HealNET 98.0 +/- 1.2; CustOmics 98.3 +/- 1.0. WSI Only block: DeepSets 68.6 +/- 4.1; AttnMIL 71.2 +/- 4.9; DeepAttnMISL 71.1 +/- 3.3; MCAT 72.3 +/- 3.3; SurvPATH 72.8 +/- 3.2; HealNET 72.9 +/- 3.2; CustOmics 73.2 +/- 3.1. WSI + Multi-Omics block: DeepSets 84.9 +/- 2.0; AttnMIL 86.6 +/- 2.1; DeepAttnMISL 88.3 +/- 2.7; MCAT 95.4 +/- 2.0; SurvPATH 96.5 +/- 1.8; HealNET 98.5 +/- 1.2; CustOmics 98.7 +/- 1.1. The AUC averaging method (macro? one-vs-rest?) is NR - the paper says only 'Area Under ROC Curve (AUC)'. Also TCGA-BRCA survival C-index, CustOmics (WSI + Multi-Omics) 65.2 +/- 3.6 (Table 2). S3 TABLE, the modality-combination ablation, downloaded as XLSX from the PLOS supplementary endpoint .s003 (HTTP 200) and parsed cell by cell, values as SNN / CustOmics: CNV 74.3 +/- 3.0 / 75.1 +/- 2.7; RNAseq 94.0 +/- 2.6 / 96.0 +/- 1.4; Methyl 81.1 +/- 1.7 / 96.0 +/- 1.4; CNV + RNAseq 94.3 +/- 2.9 / 96.9 +/- 0.8; CNV + Methyl 81.4 +/- 1.8 / 85.7 +/- 2.1; RNAseq + methyl 93.2 +/- 1.0 / 97.3 +/- 0.7; CNV + RNAseq + Methyl 94.1 +/- 2.7 / 98.9 +/- 1.4. CRITICAL SPLIT-TYPE FACT: the S3 Table caption pins those seven rows to a DIFFERENT TASK - 'Performance comparison between multiple combination of modalities for Multimodal CustOmics for the Pancancer classification task. The evaluation is done using the Area Under ROC-curve (AUC).' They are pan-cancer tumour-type numbers, NOT BRCA PAM50 numbers, and must never be quoted as a CNV-alone PAM50 result.
rows.external_validation: NONE for the BRCA subtype task, confirmed on full text. The only non-TCGA cohort in the paper is IALT, and it is NSCLC used for SURVIVAL interpretability: 'To validate the interpretability results provided by our method, we employed a private validation dataset derived from the International Adjuvant Lung Cancer Trial (IALT). This study included patients with non-small-cell lung cancer... The validation entails predicting survival outcomes using histopathology slides and DNAseq data.' Every other IALT mention in the text is in the LUAD/LUSC survival-interpretability results or the S2 Table caption. The BRCA PAM50 numbers are 5-fold CV on TCGA only.
rows.code: https://github.com/HakimBenkirane/Multimodal-CustOmics - stated in the Data availability statement, said to include preprocessing pipelines, model architecture and training scripts.
rows.caveats: THE DECISIVE FINDING ON THE LEAKAGE QUESTION, and it is sharper than 'no ablation exists'. A CNV-WITHOUT-RNA-seq arm DOES exist in S3 Table (CNV alone 75.1 against RNAseq alone 96.0 for CustOmics), but the S3 caption pins it to the PANCANCER tumour-type task, not to BRCA PAM50. FOR THE BRCA PAM50 ENDPOINT THERE IS NO NON-LEAKY ARM: every BRCA number in Table 1 that beats the WSI-only 73.2 has RNA-seq in the bag, and under this project's own rule - PAM50 labels are computed from the expression matrix - the 98.3 and 98.7 figures are target-leaking by construction. Second caveat: the class count is NR and the word PAM50 appears once in the whole paper, so it is not even established from the table itself whether the BRCA task is 4-class or 5-class. Third: the CNV representation is deliberately NOT arm-level - 'CNV data as segment mean values... All features are mapped to gene-level representations using standard annotations: CNVs via UCSC genome browser coordinates' - and the resulting CNV feature count is never stated anywhere, so it is not shallow-WGS-reachable in the sense 39 arm medians are. Refereed. HOW TO USE IT: context only for the headline numbers, and a fair comparator for exactly one thing - its WSI-only arm. CustOmics (WSI Only) 73.2 +/- 3.1 AUC% on TCGA-BRCA subtypes, 5-fold CV, patient level, sits far below this project's internal WSI-only 0.887, but the class set is unknown (possibly 5-class with Normal-like) and the AUC averaging is unstated, so the gap is not interpretable as a like-for-like margin. Its 98.7 is NOT a comparator to any fusion number here: internal-only 5-fold CV on TCGA with RNA-seq inside the bag and PAM50 labels derived from that same expression matrix. Its real value is as a full-text counter-example to 'Amer 2025 is the only WSI+CNV PAM50 work', and as the cleanest illustration that the field's high PAM50 fusion numbers come from RNA and not from CNV - on the only task where CNV is separated out at all, CNV alone gives 75.1 against RNAseq alone 96.0.

rows.title: Genome-Anchored Foundation Model Embeddings Improve Molecular Prediction from Histology Images
rows.authors: Cheng Jin, Fengtao Zhou, Yunfang Yu, Jiabo Ma, Yihui Wang, Yingxue Xu, Huajun Zhou, Hao Jiang, Luyang Luo, Luhui Mao, Zifan He, Xiuming Zhang, Jing Zhang, Ronald Cheong Kin Chan, Herui Yao, Hao Chen. The method is named PathLUPI; that acronym is not part of the registered title, which carries no parenthetical suffix in either the arXiv or the Crossref record.
rows.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2506.19681v1 [cs.CV], submitted 24 June 2025. UNREFEREED. The arXiv API confirms v1 is still the only version (published and updated both 2025-06-24T14:48:12Z); no journal version was located.
rows.modalities: H&E WSI at inference; bulk transcriptomics as PRIVILEGED INFORMATION during training only. Confirmed verbatim in three independent places: abstract, 'uses transcriptomic privileged information during training to extract genome-anchored histological embeddings, enabling effective molecular prediction using only WSIs at inference'; results, 'During inference, only the optimized distillation branch is activated for predictions'; methods, 'Inference. During inference, only the distilled branch is activated.' There is NO copy-number modality anywhere in the paper.
rows.datasets: TCGA across 13 solid cancer types for all internal tasks; external cohorts are Center-1 (N = 1,527), Center-2 (2,045 patients on the BRCA-Mol* task per Extended Data Table 5), CPTAC (N = 406) and EBRAINS (N = 852). 49 molecular oncology tasks, 11,257 cases, 20 cohorts in total. The two BRCA subtyping tasks are BRCA-Mol (505 patients, TCGA) and BRCA-Mol* (2,045 patients, Center-2).
rows.endpoint: Molecular subtyping (8 tasks), plus actionable and investigational biomarker prediction and survival. CLASS COUNT for both BRCA tasks: 4, established from the class list in Extended Data Table 5, 'Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-enriched, Basal-like', for both the internal and the external row. Normal-like is absent, matching this project's exclusion. The enumeration is a real one rather than a formatting artefact: the same table lists 5 classes for GBMLGG-Mol ('G-CIMP-high, G-CIMP-low, Codel, Mesenchymal-like, Classic-like') and 4 for CRC-Mol and HNSC-Mol. PREDICTION UNIT: case/patient - 'These tasks were defined based on biologically meaningful patient-level labels... Labels were matched to TCGA patient IDs, and for patients with multiple WSIs, slide-level features were aggregated into patient-level representations', and Extended Data Table 5 is headed 'Task ID (Patient Count)'. LABEL BASIS, INTERNAL: RNA-derived PAM50 via TCGAbiolinks - 'Molecular subtype tasks were derived using TCGAbiolinks, including PAM50 status for BRCA, and CMS status for colorectal cancer'; the underlying caller inside TCGAbiolinks is not named. LABEL BASIS, EXTERNAL (BRCA-Mol*, Center-2): NR, and this is the single most important unknown in the row - Extended Data Table 5 gives Label Type 'Molecular Subtype', the same four class names, and Label Source 'Center-2', with no assay named anywhere.
rows.wsi_pipeline: Verbatim: 'Each slide W(s)_i is divided into non-overlapping patches of size 512x512 pixels at 20x magnification. We use the CONCH foundation model, a pathology-specific pretrained encoder, to extract patch-level embeddings v(s)_j in R^dv ... dv = 512'. A region-aware re-embedding transformer refines them. Dual branch - a privileged transcriptomic branch and a distilled WSI branch - with attention-map and representation alignment losses, and gated attention pooling to a slide-level vector. Multi-slide cases: 'Each WSI in W_i is independently processed into patch-level features, which are subsequently concatenated across all slides to form a unified image representation for the case.' Patching and heatmaps use the CLAM toolbox.
rows.fusion_method: Not a fusion model in the multimodal-at-inference sense - it is learning using privileged information (LUPI) by knowledge distillation. Transcriptomics conditions the training objective and is absent at test time.
rows.metrics: Extended Data Table 3, 'Performance of molecular subtyping. Best-performing model for each metric is in bold. * denotes external cohorts.' Values are mean (95% CI) across columns ABMIL / CLAM / DTFD / TransMIL / PathLUPI. BRCA, INTERNAL, TCGA, n=505: AUC 0.867 (0.866-0.868) / 0.867 (0.866-0.868) / 0.858 (0.858-0.859) / 0.852 (0.851-0.853) / 0.876 (0.876-0.877); ACC 0.689 (0.688-0.690) / 0.689 (0.688-0.690) / 0.664 (0.663-0.665) / 0.642 (0.641-0.643) / 0.676 (0.675-0.677); F1 0.633 (0.631-0.635) / 0.614 (0.612-0.616) / 0.602 (0.600-0.603) / 0.516 (0.515-0.518) / 0.606 (0.605-0.608). BRCA*, EXTERNAL, Center-2, n=2,045: AUC 0.701 (0.701-0.702) / 0.706 (0.705-0.706) / 0.666 (0.666-0.667) / 0.710 (0.710-0.710) / 0.727 (0.726-0.727); ACC 0.425 (0.424-0.426) / 0.425 (0.425-0.426) / 0.354 (0.353-0.355) / 0.485 (0.485-0.486) / 0.491 (0.490-0.493); F1 0.355 (0.354-0.356) / 0.357 (0.356-0.357) / 0.260 (0.259-0.261) / 0.416 (0.416-0.417) / 0.450 (0.449-0.452). Aggregate text: internal subtyping 'mean AUC of 0.856, representing a 1.47% improvement over the best-performing baseline (P < 0.001)'; external 'a mean AUC of 0.727, surpassing the strongest comparator by 2.4% (P < 0.001)' - note BRCA-Mol* is the only starred task in the eight-task subtyping panel, so that external mean coincides with PathLUPI's BRCA* cell. SPLIT TYPE, verbatim: 'Each task-specific model was trained using five-fold cross-validation with an 80:20 train-validation split. For evaluation on external datasets, we applied each of the five cross-validation models independently and reported the average of their performance metrics... Performance metrics were estimated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples to compute means and 95% confidence intervals (CIs).' Significance by one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank. Survival, Extended Data Table 4: BRCA C-index CLAM 0.668 (0.666-0.670), PathLUPI 0.710 (0.708-0.712); BRCA* C-index CLAM 0.622 (0.621-0.622), PathLUPI 0.641 (0.640-0.641). AVERAGING SCHEME UNVERIFIABLE FROM THE PAPER: the multiclass AUC averaging is never defined - grep counts over the complete extracted full text return 'macro' = 0 occurrences and 'one-vs-rest / one-vs-all / ovr' = 0 occurrences.
rows.external_validation: YES, genuinely held out and never trained on. BRCA-Mol* (2,045 patients) comes from Center-2, a private institutional cohort; the five TCGA-trained CV models are applied without retraining and averaged. Verbatim: 'All external datasets were processed using the same pipeline as TCGA to ensure consistency in feature extraction and label definition.' Useful independent cross-check on CPTAC-BRCA cohort size: BRCA-PIK3CA* (116) and BRCA-TP53* (116), both with Label Source 'CPTAC (cBioPortal)'.
rows.code: NR - no repository URL appears anywhere in the retrieved text.
rows.caveats: UNREFEREED PREPRINT (arXiv:2506.19681v1, 24 June 2025; v1 is the only version and no journal version was found). THE DECISIVE GAP: the Center-2 label basis for BRCA-Mol* is never stated. Extended Data Table 5 gives Label Type 'Molecular Subtype', the four class names and Label Source 'Center-2', and that is all. The Methods sentence that establishes PAM50 covers only the TCGA side. The only bridge to the external side is 'All external datasets were processed using the same pipeline as TCGA to ensure consistency in feature extraction and label definition', which asserts consistency without describing an assay. A 2,045-patient RNA-derived PAM50 assay in a single private hospital cohort is implausible; an IHC surrogate mapped onto the same four class names is far more likely, and would make BRCA-Mol* NOT a PAM50 external evaluation. RECORDED AS NR, EXPLICITLY, and the external 0.727 therefore cannot be audited. Second gap: the AUC averaging method is undefined (macro and one-vs-rest both absent from the text). Third: the patch encoder is CONCH (512-dim, 512x512 px at 20x), not UNI2-h (1536-dim, 256 px at 20x), so its CLAM baseline is not this project's CLAM baseline. HOW TO USE IT: near comparator needing a caveat - the sharpest external-generalisation comparator in this batch and the strongest challenge to the claim that no published multimodal PAM50 model has an external never-trained-on PAM50-specific evaluation. It DENTS rather than BREAKS that claim, for two independent reasons: inference is WSI-only, so it is not a multimodal external evaluation; and the external label basis is NR and quite possibly not PAM50. Against this project's numbers, the quotable contrast is the transport gap: its CLAM baseline falls 0.867 internal (TCGA, n=505) to 0.706 external (Center-2, n=2,045), a drop of 0.161, while CLAM-MB + UNI2-h here falls 0.887 internal (TCGA, 599 cases) to 0.847 external (CPTAC, n=114), a drop of 0.040. That contrast must carry its caveats - different encoders, different external cohorts, undefined AUC averaging on their side, and CPTAC's stage IIA-IIIC eligibility and absent Normal-like already making it an easier external target.

rows.title: A Unified Genetic and Epigenetic Model to Predict Breast Cancer Intrinsic Subtypes Using Large DNA-Level Multi-Omics Data and Hierarchical Learning (UGES)
rows.authors: X. Chang, J. Xie, H. Duan, K. Li, X. Liu, Y. Xiong, X. Bai, K. Ning, L. C. Xia (PubMed author string; Crossref expands the last to Xia Li C.). The earlier bioRxiv version lists a DIFFERENT author set - Jiemin Xie, Binyu Yang, Keyi Li, Lixin Gao, Xuemei Liu, Yunhui Xiong, Wen Chen, Li C. Xia - so the author list changed between preprint and journal version.
rows.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics 2025 Nov-Dec;22(6):3000-3016. Refereed. PMID 40986589, DOI 10.1109/TCBBIO.2025.3613591, IEEE Xplore document 11176992; pagination confirmed independently from PubMed and Crossref. Earlier preprint: bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.06.12.544702 (13 June 2023), titled 'Building a genetic and epigenetic predictive model of breast cancer intrinsic subtypes using large-scale data and hierarchical structure learning'.
rows.modalities: DNA-level multi-omics only: somatic mutations plus copy number aberrations plus DNA methylation. NO imaging modality. NO gene expression as an input, stated explicitly in the Limitations - 'unlike the typical approach that uses expression data, UGES was developed using only DNA alterations.' Transcription data was downloaded alongside the rest but is not among the 50,831 features.
rows.datasets: TCGA n=931 plus METABRIC n=1134, total 2,065 samples, from cBioPortal and the TCGA data portal. Three cohort configurations are defined: TCGA-only, METABRIC-only, and combined TCGA+METABRIC.
rows.endpoint: 4-class breast cancer intrinsic subtype via a three-step hierarchical classifier encoded in Newick notation as (B,(H,(LA,LB))) - Basal split off first, then Her2, then LumA vs LumB. CLASS COUNT: 4, established from the Newick encodings and their gloss ('where B, H, LA, and LB denote the Basal, Her2, Lum-A, and -B subtypes'), corroborated by the training design ('we randomly selected 200 samples from each subtype, resulting in a total of 800 samples for training') and by the four per-subtype test AUCs. Normal-like is excluded, matching this project's class set exactly. PREDICTION UNIT: case/patient, i.e. one tumour sample with DNA-level omics; no imaging, so no patch or slide question arises. LABEL BASIS: RNA-derived PAM50 used as training labels, verbatim - 'We used PAM50 subtypes as the initial training labels to construct the UGES classifier despite the fact that accurately determining the true intrinsic subtypes of breast cancer experimentally is challenging. We opted for the PAM50 label because it is one of the most internationally recognized for classifying intrinsic subtypes.' The caller is NR, and - importantly - HOW THE LABELS WERE HARMONISED ACROSS TCGA AND METABRIC IS NEVER STATED, although the two cohorts use different PAM50 assignment pipelines.
rows.wsi_pipeline: N/A - no imaging.
rows.fusion_method: Not multimodal fusion in the imaging sense. Hierarchical multi-step classification: at each node a set of one-vs-rest Lasso-Logistic regression classifiers (glmnet, 10-fold CV to pick lambda) over the concatenated 50,831 DNA features. The integration is plain early concatenation of the three DNA assay types.
rows.metrics: CNA GRANULARITY, verbatim: 'For CNA, we used the downloaded absolute copy number values, as estimated by the TCGA consortium and mapped to the gene level by cBioPortal' - GENE LEVEL, not arm level, not segment level; independently corroborated by a negative check, since arm-level / arm level / low-pass / shallow / sWGS / whole-genome sequencing return zero hits in the manuscript. FEATURE COMPOSITION, verbatim: 'This resulted in the inclusion of 50,831 gene-level DNA features, including 16,770 mutations, 25,594 CNAs, and 8,467 methylation features.' HEADLINE NUMBERS, all on the POOLED TCGA+METABRIC test set (n=1,265) unless stated, metric = overall AUC averaged over all subtypes: (B,(H,(LA,LB))) TRAIN 0.984 (n=800) / TEST 0.963; ((B,H),(LA,LB)) 0.991/0.952; (B,H,(LA,LB)) 0.984/0.956; one-step (B,H,LA,LB) 0.965/0.889. Per-subtype TEST AUC for the selected (B,(H,(LA,LB))): Basal 0.987, Her2 0.974, LumA 0.96, LumB 0.933; for ((B,H),(LA,LB)) 0.991/0.956/0.953/0.909; for (B,H,(LA,LB)) 0.992/0.94/0.96/0.933; for one-step 0.988/0.935/0.852/0.782. SINGLE-ALTERATION ABLATION on the same pooled test set: mutation-only 0.7, CNA-ONLY 0.877, methylation-only 0.935, against multi-omics 0.963. One-vs-one LumA-vs-LumB AUC: one-step 0.828, (B,(H,(LA,LB))) 0.948, ((B,H),(LA,LB)) 0.941, (B,H,(LA,LB)) 0.951. Against XAI-MethylMarker on the full test set: 0.963 vs 0.898. Against moBRCA-net on the TCGA PART of the test set only: accuracy 0.9154 vs 0.891, weighted F1 0.921 vs 0.887, MCC 0.8487 vs 0.831. THE IMPROVEMENT CLAIM IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, both readings quoted and neither reconciled: the abstract and Introduction say 'improving the overall AUC score by over 8.3% compared to the one-step multi-classification method' (a relative change, 0.963 vs 0.889), while the Results body says 'a substantial improvement in the overall AUC by at least 6.3% compared to the one-step strategy model'; the bioRxiv preprint abstract states the same improvement as 0.074 absolute. AUC AVERAGING: 'overall AUC scores (averaged over all subtypes)', i.e. an unweighted mean of per-subtype one-vs-rest AUCs - macro-like, though the word macro is never used; a separate one-vs-one analysis is in Supplementary Fig. S1. Survival stratification p-values: P = 9.7e-55 (UGES) vs 2.2e-47 (PAM50).
rows.external_validation: THE HEADLINE 0.963 HAS NO HELD-OUT EXTERNAL COHORT - METABRIC IS POOLED INTO TRAINING. Verbatim: 'We divided the TCGA+METABRIC cohorts into training and test sets (Fig. 1c). To ensure balanced representation of the four intrinsic subtypes in the training set, we randomly selected 200 samples from each subtype, resulting in a total of 800 samples for training, with the remaining 1,265 samples used as the test set.' BUT genuine cross-cohort arms DO exist, in Supplementary Fig. S3, verbatim: 'When UGES model was trained solely on METABRIC and tested on TCGA, the overall AUC on the test set was 0.735. In the reverse scenario, when UGES was trained on TCGA and tested on METABRIC, the overall AUC improved to 0.846.' The authors attribute the drop to batch effect and domain shift. Those two figures, not the 0.963, are the external result.
rows.code: https://github.com/labxscut/UGES - stated in the abstract and in the Data Availability Statement.
rows.caveats: EVIDENCE PROVENANCE - STATE THIS WHEREVER THE PAPER IS CITED: the full text read for this row is the AUTHOR MANUSCRIPT, not the IEEE version of record. IEEE Xplore could not be reached - curl -L on https://doi.org/10.1109/TCBBIO.2025.3613591 returned HTTP 202 at https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11176992/ (a bot interstitial) and WebFetch on that URL returned an empty body; paper-search read pubmed 40986589 returns only the abstract by design. The text read is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/labxscut/UGES/HEAD/Final_Manuscript.md (HTTP 200), the authors' own accepted manuscript on the paper's GitHub repository, whose title, nine-author list and abstract match the published record exactly. Every number reported here that also appears in the PubMed abstract was cross-checked against it and matched (50831 features, 2065 samples, AUC 0.963, P = 9.7e-55 vs 2.2e-47, 8.3%). Numbers NOT in the abstract - the per-subtype AUCs, the CNA-only 0.877, the 0.9154/0.921/0.8487 triple, the cross-cohort 0.735/0.846 and the METABRIC-pooling sentence - rest on that manuscript alone, and section labels such as 'Results section B' are the manuscript's, not the journal's. SECOND KEY FACT: NO ctDNA OR LOW-COVERAGE ASSAY WAS EVER USED. ctDNA appears only as motivation in the Introduction and as future work in a Discussion paragraph that lists three obstacles; the sentence 'the data used to train UGES comes from solid tumor samples' opens the paragraph AFTER that one, not within it. The Limitations also concede 'we have not yet considered chromosomal-level structural changes', which is exactly the scale 39 arm medians occupy. HOW TO USE IT: near comparator needing a caveat - this is the number a reviewer will throw at a CNV-only 0.888 external / 0.866 internal, and it must be defused precisely rather than dismissed. Three facts defuse it. (1) THE POOLING: the 0.963 is a within-pool test split, not an external cohort; the paper's own genuine cross-cohort arms land at 0.735 (METABRIC to TCGA) and 0.846 (TCGA to METABRIC), BOTH BELOW this project's 0.888 external CPTAC figure, which is the comparison that actually matters. (2) THE FEATURE SET IS NOT sWGS-REACHABLE: 25,594 gene-level CNAs plus 16,770 mutations plus 8,467 methylation features, against 39 arm medians; the ctDNA motivation is aspirational only. (3) THE ONE GENUINELY APPLES-TO-APPLES ARM IS ITS CNA-ONLY ABLATION - 0.877 overall AUC on the pooled TCGA+METABRIC test set from 25,594 gene-level CNAs, against 0.866 +/- 0.003 internal / 0.888 external from 39 arms. That is the strongest single datapoint anywhere that arm-level coarsening costs almost nothing, and it - not the 0.963 - should be the reported comparator, caveated with the different cohorts, the different split design, the unstated cross-cohort label harmonisation and the macro-like averaging the paper never names.

rows.title: Clinical Validation of the Belay Ascent(TM) Test to Report on Chromosomal Arm-Level Aneuploidy and Gene-Level Copy Number Variants in Cerebrospinal Fluid Using Low-Pass Whole-Genome Sequencing
rows.authors: Qian Nie, Kala F. Schilter, Alexandra Larson, Vindhya Udhane, Viriya Keo, Sakshi Khurana, Jennifer N. Adams, Anthony Acevedo, Daniel Sanchez, Tarin Peltier, Kathleen Mitchell, DeElegant Robinson, Kyle M. Hernandez, Christopher Douville, Chetan Bettegowda, Honey V. Reddi (Belay Diagnostics, Chicago IL; Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine)
rows.venue: Cancers (MDPI) 2026, 18(8), 1277, published 17 April 2026 (received 13 March 2026, revised 8 April 2026, accepted 11 April 2026). Refereed, open access. Record confirmed via the Europe PMC REST API: single hit, PMID 42073600 / PMC13115066 / doi 10.3390/cancers18081277, Cancers vol 18 issue 8, isOpenAccess Y.
rows.modalities: Single modality: low-pass whole-genome sequencing of tumour-derived DNA in cerebrospinal fluid. No imaging, no expression, no fusion.
rows.datasets: 323 unique specimens in total. Equivalence cohort: 48 tissue specimens (45 FFPE primary CNS tumours plus 3 products-of-conception tissues). Validation cohort: 32 CSF specimens with matched tissue-based tumour profiling, comprising 4 primary and 28 metastatic CNS cancers (16 breast, 10 lung, 1 esophageal, 1 sarcoma). Production cohort: 243 Ascent-positive specimens, drawn from 867 received for clinical testing, of which 345 were negative for both tests, 233 Ascent-negative/Summit-positive, 16 failed testing and 275 Ascent-positive.
rows.endpoint: Assay concordance (positive and negative percent agreement) for detecting chromosome ARM-LEVEL aneuploidy and gene-level CNVs, plus clinical impact on WHO diagnosis, actionability and prognosis in CNS cancers. This is NOT a molecular-subtype classifier of any kind and NOT breast cancer - breast appears only as 16 metastatic CNS cases in the validation cohort. CLASS COUNT: NR and not applicable; the assay reports arm-level gain/loss calls and gene-level CNV calls, not class labels. PREDICTION UNIT: specimen, one CSF or tissue specimen per result - but concordance is additionally computed per EVENT (25 of 25 aneuploidy events, 34 of 35 gene-level CNVs, 7 of 9, 34 of 38), so the denominators mix specimens and events and must always be quoted with their units. LABEL BASIS: other - the reference standard is matched tissue-based tumour profiling by CMA, NGS, FISH and IHC, with selected gene-level calls (ERBB2 amplification, EGFR amplification, CDKN2A/2B deletion) additionally confirmed by clinically validated gene-specific qPCR. No molecular-subtype label of any kind.
rows.wsi_pipeline: N/A - no imaging.
rows.fusion_method: N/A - single assay, no model fusion.
rows.metrics: ASSAY OUTPUT, abstract verbatim: 'The Belay Ascent(TM) liquid biopsy test uses low-pass whole-genome sequencing (LP-WGS) to report on chromosome arm-level aneuploidy and gene-level copy number variants (CNVs) in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).' ANALYTICAL VALIDATION, cited to a prior publication (ref [46]) and NOT newly established here: 'Analytical validation of Ascent for calling chromosome arm-level aneuploidy at an abs(log2r) threshold of 0.09 demonstrated a sensitivity/PPA of 91% and a specificity/NPA of 99%, with a limit of input of >=20 ng of CSF tDNA.' EQUIVALENCE COHORT, 48 tissue specimens against CMA/NGS: arm-level aneuploidy 25 of 25 events detected = 100% PPA; gene-level CNVs 34 of 35 = 97% PPA; NPA 100% across the 9 negative specimens; the 3 products-of-conception specimens with complex genotypes yielded 84 arm-level aneuploidy events detected. VALIDATION COHORT, 32 CSF specimens: arm-level aneuploidy 7 of 9 events in two CSF specimens detected = 78% PPA; gene-level CNVs 27 of 31 against NGS = 87% PPA, 4 of 4 against IHC = 100%, 3 of 3 against FISH = 100%, 'for an overall PPA of 89% (detecting 34 of 38 events total) for gene-level CNVs'; NPA 100% across 8 specimens with no known events. INTERNAL DISCREPANCY, quoted both ways and not reconciled: the abstract states '78% and 90% PPA for aneuploidy and gene-level CNVs, respectively' while the Results body computes 89% (34 of 38). PRODUCTION: 243 of 275 Ascent-positive specimens evaluated for clinical significance; chromosomal instability, defined as more than 5 arm-level events, was observed in 73% (22 of 30 specimens). GENE-LEVEL CALL THRESHOLDS: seg.mean >=0.1 for gain, <=0 to <0.1 for no change, >=-0.2 for loss, all confirmed against clinically validated gene-specific qPCR.
rows.external_validation: N/A in the model sense. The design is an equivalence cohort (tissue, against a CMA/NGS gold standard), then an independent clinical validation cohort (CSF, against matched tissue-based profiling), then a real-world production cohort - three distinct specimen sets, with no model trained and therefore nothing pooled.
rows.code: NR - a commercial laboratory-developed test; no code released.
rows.caveats: ACCESS NOTE: the DOI does not resolve for automated clients - https://doi.org/10.3390/cancers18081277 returns HTTP 403 at https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6694/18/8/1277 (MDPI/Cloudflare bot block, reproduced with curl). The full text was read through Europe PMC (PMID 42073600 / PMC13115066, HTTP 200, open access CC BY). Refereed. WRONG DISEASE AND WRONG ENDPOINT for any direct comparison - CNS tumour diagnosis and management, not breast, not molecular subtype. TWO THINGS ARE SIMPLY NOT IN THE PAPER. (a) The SEQUENCING COVERAGE DEPTH is never given numerically: 'low-pass' and 'LP-WGS' are used throughout with no read depth, no genome-equivalents figure and no coverage value for the Ascent assay anywhere. There are four coverage-adjacent sentences in the text, but all four concern comparator methods or are generic - the FAST-SeqS description 'By evaluating the read depth at each locus', 'its genome coverage is limited to predefined loci', 'higher coverage at the loci queried', and 'compared to high coverage approaches'. (b) NO COST, NO TURNAROUND TIME AND NO REIMBURSEMENT STATUS is stated. 'Cost-effective, quick detection of key biomarkers' in the comparison table belongs to the IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY row, not to Belay Ascent - Belay's own row lists the advantage 'Low input DNA (<20 ng)' and the limitation 'Longer turnaround times compared to IHC and FISH'; the only cost sentence in the paper is the qualitative Discussion line 'Low-pass sequencing reduces per-sample sequencing costs compared to high coverage approaches'. So this paper makes the cheapness claim CLINICALLY REAL but NOT QUANTITATIVE. The only tumour-fraction figure is a literature citation rather than their own measurement: 'It is worth noting that LP-WGS usually requires a tumor fraction of 1-5% to reliably call aneuploidies in tissue [73].' Conflict-of-interest context: the assay is the sponsoring company's own product and 15 of 16 authors are Belay Diagnostics employees. HOW TO USE IT: context only, but the most load-bearing piece of context in this batch for the DESIGN RATIONALE half of the story rather than for any number. It shares no endpoint, no disease and no metric with this project. What it does is convert 'arm-level CNV is cheap and clinically reachable' from a modelling convenience into a documented fact - a deployed, clinically validated, in-production LP-WGS assay whose literal reported output is chromosome ARM-LEVEL aneuploidy, with 243 real production cases behind it and 100% PPA against CMA for arm-level calls in tissue. Cite it for that and only that, carrying two caveats: coverage depth and cost are both unstated, so it supports the reachability claim without quantifying the cheapness claim; and it is CSF/CNS, so transfer to a breast sWGS setting is by analogy.

rows.title: Systematic comparison of multi-omics survival models reveals a widespread lack of noise resistance
rows.authors: David Wissel, Daniel Rowson, Valentina Boeva
rows.venue: Cell Reports Methods 3, 100461, published 24 April 2023. Refereed, open access. Record confirmed via the Europe PMC REST API: PMID 37159669, PMC10162996, doi 10.1016/j.crmeth.2023.100461.
rows.modalities: Seven molecular and clinical modalities, NO IMAGING: 'we chose only datasets that had available all modalities of interest, namely, clinical data, gene expression, protein expression, Copy Number Variation (CNV), methylation, mutation, and micro-RNA'.
rows.datasets: 17 TCGA datasets. Verbatim: 'In our study, we considered 17 datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA).' Preprocessed from PANCANATLAS except CNV, which was taken from Xenabrowser. The identities of the 17 cancer types live in Table S1/S3 (XLSX) and are NOT enumerated in the article text; ESCA, HNSC and LUSC are named exemplarily in figure captions.
rows.endpoint: Overall survival as per Liu et al. Not a classification task and not a subtype task. CLASS COUNT: NR and not applicable (survival endpoint scored by Antolini's C and the Integrated Brier Score). PREDICTION UNIT: case/patient - TCGA survival endpoints are patient-level throughout; the nearest explicit sentence, 'we summed the five test predictions for each patient (since we repeated our cross-validations five times)', comes from the Kaplan-Meier-curve construction subsection rather than from a general statement about the evaluation unit, so it is weaker support than it looks. LABEL BASIS: other - overall survival time and event status, 'as per Liu et al.' (the TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource). No molecular subtype is involved anywhere.
rows.wsi_pipeline: N/A - no imaging modality anywhere in the study.
rows.fusion_method: Twelve methods compared: four statistical (BlockForest, PriorityLasso, RSF, Elastic net) and eight deep-learning fusion variants (Early; Intermediate with Attention / Concat / Embrace / Max / Mean pooling; Late with Mean / MoE). LATE-FUSION DEFINITION, verbatim: 'Lastly, for late fusion, we distinguish Late (Mean) and Late (MoE), which respectively use a mean pooling and a weighted mean (based on a gating network) operation to fuse the partial hazards predictions of each modality network.'
rows.metrics: TABLE 1 IN FULL, caption verbatim: 'All considered methods showed a lack of noise resistance, exemplified by their inability to outperform the clinical baselines'; sub-caption: 'Mean Antolini's C and IBS across test splits and datasets when integrating clinical data and gene expression compared to integrating all of the available modalities (described in Table S1). Standard errors are in parentheses. * indicates values that were not significantly worse than the best model per column.' Columns are [Antolini's C: Clinical+GEX, All] then [IBS: Clinical+GEX, All]. BlockForest 0.637 (0.0059)*,c | 0.619 (0.0060)* | 0.162 (0.0020)*,c,d | 0.164 (0.0021)*,d. Elastic net 0.599 (0.0061)c | 0.589 (0.0060) | 0.167 (0.0021) | 0.168 (0.0021). PriorityLasso 0.632 (0.0060)*,c | 0.626 (0.0063)* | 0.166 (0.0022)c | 0.174 (0.0024). RSF 0.601 (0.0055)c | 0.575 (0.0059) | 0.167 (0.0020)c | 0.169 (0.0021). Early 0.607 (0.0058)c | 0.587 (0.0059) | 0.176 (0.0025)c | 0.179 (0.0025). Intermediate (Attention) 0.633 (0.0057)*,c | 0.616 (0.0055) | 0.173 (0.0026) | 0.177 (0.0026). Intermediate (Concat) 0.635 (0.0057)*,c | 0.624 (0.0053)* | 0.173 (0.0026)c | 0.190 (0.0035). Intermediate (Embrace) 0.622 (0.0056)*,c | 0.575 (0.0057) | 0.172 (0.0024)c | 0.182 (0.0026). Intermediate (Max) 0.635 (0.0055)*,c | 0.602 (0.0056) | 0.174 (0.0025)c | 0.186 (0.0027). Intermediate (Mean) 0.636 (0.0054)*,c | 0.615 (0.0056) | 0.171 (0.0023)c | 0.176 (0.0025). LATE (MEAN) 0.631 (0.0056)* | 0.627 (0.0054)* | 0.172 (0.0025) | 0.171 (0.0023). LATE (MoE) 0.599 (0.0056)c | 0.564 (0.0054) | 0.179 (0.0024)c | 0.188 (0.0034). Late (MoE)'s 0.564 is the minimum of the twelve All-column values, checked directly. Footnotes verbatim: 'a denotes a metric for which higher values are better. b the opposite. c indicates significantly better performance for a model utilizing clinical data and gene expression compared to all available modalities. P values are based on paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, except for the unimodal comparison, which is based on two-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. d indicates significantly better performance than the best clinical-only model.' SPLIT TYPE: 'For all datasets in our experiments, we performed outer 5-fold cross-validation, five times repeated, stratified on the event indicator, giving us a total of 25 test splits per dataset.' Abstract verbatim: 'we compared eight deep learning and four statistical integration techniques for survival prediction on 17 multi-omics datasets... We found that one deep learning method, mean late fusion, and two statistical methods, PriorityLasso and BlockForest, performed best in terms of both noise resistance and overall discriminative and calibration performance.' Results verbatim: 'All of our considered models except Late (Mean) performed significantly worse in terms of Antolini's C when integrating all available modalities compared with clinical data and gene expression (Table 1).' AND, corrected here from a mis-transcription that dropped both the condition and half the comparator, the sentence about the three worst methods reads in full: 'When integrating one noise modality, Intermediate (Embrace), Late (MoE), and RSF performed significantly worse in terms of Antolini's C compared to using only clinical data and gene expression.' That is the Table 3 Gaussian-noise-injection experiment, not the Table 1 setting, and the comparator is the Clinical+GEX model, NOT a clinical-only baseline.
rows.external_validation: N/A - no external cohort. All 17 datasets are TCGA and all evaluation is 5-times-repeated 5-fold CV (25 test splits per dataset) within each dataset. Nothing is pooled across cancer types for training.
rows.code: A repository is referenced in the STAR Methods ('The repository also contains links to the splits, datasets as well as all of our results'); the URL itself did not survive the PDF-to-text extraction, so the address is NR from this retrieval.
rows.caveats: NO WHOLE-SLIDE-IMAGE MODALITY ANYWHERE - confirmed by the explicit seven-modality list in the Datasets section and by grep: 'whole-slide' returns exactly one hit, the related-work sentence about Cheerla and Gevaert; 'WSI' returns zero. ('histological type' does occur once, but as a shared clinical covariate, not an imaging modality.) The endpoint is survival scored by Antolini's C and IBS, so NOTHING here converts to an AUROC. D-CAL IS NOT IN THIS PAPER: the calibration metric is the Integrated Brier Score, and grepping for D-CAL and D-calibration returns zero hits; recorded as NR. The 17 dataset identities live in Table S1/S3 (XLSX) and are not in the article text. RETRIEVAL NOTE: PMC10162996 could NOT be read - both paper-search read pmc PMC10162996 and read europepmc PMC10162996 fail with 'does not have an open access PDF'; the working route is by PMID, paper-search read europepmc PMID:37159669. Refereed. HOW TO USE IT: near comparator needing a caveat, and the single strongest published precedent for the fusion-operator result here, but on a different endpoint and with no imaging. It maps on with unusual precision at the level of operator ORDERING rather than values: their Late (Mean), an untrained mean over per-modality predictions, is the ONLY method of twelve that does not degrade significantly when modalities are added (0.631 -> 0.627 Antolini's C), while their Late (MoE), a LEARNED GATE over exactly the same per-modality predictions, is the WORST of all twelve in both settings (0.599 -> 0.564) and degrades the most. That is an independent probability-mean-beats-gated result on multi-omics survival. It also supports the second half of the story: every jointly trained intermediate operator degrades under added modalities while the untrained late mean does not, which is consistent with an error-correlation mechanism - though they never measure error correlation, so that mechanistic link is an inference here and not their finding. MANDATORY CAVEATS when citing: no WSI modality anywhere; none of their numbers is comparable to any AUROC; their untrained-mean advantage is a NON-DEGRADATION result under noise rather than an outright win (BlockForest 0.637 edges Late (Mean) 0.631 in the Clinical+GEX setting), whereas the probability mean here genuinely beats every trained operator outright; and their headline is that no method beat the clinical-only baselines at all, which has no analogue in this project's setup.

rows.title: Multiple instance learning on tile level-pathology images provides accurate and interpretable classification for breast cancer molecular subtypes
rows.authors: Konstantinos Athanasios Papagoras, Ole Lund, Carolina Barra (Section for Bioinformatics, Department of Health Technology, Technical University of Denmark)
rows.venue: bioRxiv preprint, posted 22 December 2025. UNREFEREED - the page carries the standard banner 'preprint (which was not certified by peer review)'. Crossref confirms institution bioRxiv, type posted-content, posted [[2025,12,22]]; Europe PMC indexes it as preprint id PPR1230633.
rows.modalities: H&E WSI only - single modality. No omics, no fusion, no CNV.
rows.datasets: Three cohorts POOLED. Verbatim accounting: 'From TCGA we downloaded 1116 H&E WSIs; 971 had subtype labels (BL, HER2, LumA, LumB). From CPTAC we obtained 653 WSIs, of which 382 were subtype-labeled (BL, HER2, LumA, LumB). Slides labeled as Normal-like and those lacking labels or corrupted were excluded. Across the combined subtyped-labeled set (n=1353), LumA was the majority class (50.1%) and HER2 the minority (8.5%)... we also gathered the Warwick cohort used by the reference, comprising 88 WSIs with 80 HER2-positive slides used in our analyses.' The abstract gives the grand total as 'A total of 1433 WSIs from three public cohorts' (971+382+80). Table 1 per-class WSI counts: TCGA-BRCA (PAM50) LumA 502, LumB 221, HER2 76, BL 172, excluded '35 Normal-like, 110 lack labels, or corrupted'; CPTAC-BRCA (PAM50) LumA 176, LumB 44, HER2 39, BL 123, excluded '13 Normal-like and 258 lack labels'; HER2-Warwick (IHC) HER2 80, excluded '8 with negative HER2 expression score'; Total LumA 678, LumB 265, HER2 195, BL 295, excluded 424. Held-out test set n=287 WSIs (LumA 136, LumB 53, HER2 39, Basal 59). 12,534,150 tissue tiles ('This procedure yielded 12.534.150 tissue tiles' - European decimal notation in the original).
rows.endpoint: 4-class breast cancer molecular subtype: LumA, LumB, HER2-enriched, Basal-like. CLASS COUNT: 4, from the Introduction ('classified into four primary subtypes: Luminal A (LumA), Luminal B (LumB), HER2-enriched (HER2), and Basal-like (BL)'), from Table 1's four class columns, and from the explicit exclusion of Normal-like (35 from TCGA, 13 from CPTAC) - the same class set this project uses. PREDICTION UNIT: SLIDE. Every reported metric is on 'a held-out test set of 287 WSIs'; Tables 3 and 5 count test examples in WSIs (136 + 53 + 39 + 59 = 287); tile-level probabilities are averaged up to a SLIDE label, never a case label, and no case- or patient-level aggregation is reported anywhere. LABEL BASIS: MIXED, and that is the defect. TCGA-BRCA and CPTAC-BRCA carry RNA-derived PAM50, with Table 1's footnote defining it as 'a gene expression-based assay that classifies breast tumors into the four intrinsic molecular subtypes (LumA, LumB, HER2 and BL) using the expression patterns of 50 selected genes'; the caller is NR. Warwick carries IHC (HER2 expression score), and its 80 HER2-positive slides are pooled into the SAME HER2 class as the expression-derived HER2-enriched TCGA/CPTAC cases.
rows.wsi_pipeline: 'WSIs were tiled with the OpenSlide library at a nominal 20x magnification into non-overlapping 224 x 224 RGB patches; when a slide lacked an explicit 20x level the nearest available level was resampled to achieve a comparable microns-per-pixel resolution.' There is NO tumour-region preselection ('rather than heavy preprocessing or tumor preselection'), but tiles ARE filtered on quality and texture: discarded if more than 80% of pixels exceed grayscale intensity 230, or grayscale standard deviation below 15, or Laplacian variance below 100. 'No stain normalization or data augmentation was used'. Encoder: 'UNI-2 was used as a frozen encoder, taking as input a tile image and producing a 1536-dimensional feature embedding per tile. Each slide is represented as a bag in a matrix format [number of tiles x 1536]' - UNI-2 being 'a ViT-H/14 architecture trained with the DINOv2 self-supervised framework'. Slide representations by mean pooling the tile embeddings; the attention-MIL head maps 1536 -> 256 hidden. Scanner/resolution table: TCGA-BRCA 971 WSIs at 0.25, 0.50 um/px (variant scanners, svs); CPTAC-BRCA 382 WSIs at 0.25, 0.50 um/px (variant, svs); HER2-Warwick 80 WSIs at 0.23 um/px (NanoZoomer C9600, ndpi).
rows.fusion_method: N/A - unimodal. The classifier variants are a cosine-similarity k-NN baseline (k=3), one-vs-rest logistic regression on mean-pooled slide embeddings (with and without SMOTE, random over- and under-sampling, with and without temperature-scaling calibration), OvR LR on tile-level vectors with mean-probability aggregation, and OvR attention-based deep MIL with class-weighted cross-entropy and per-class temperature scaling.
rows.metrics: ALL SLIDE-LEVEL, all on the SAME held-out test set of 287 WSIs, which is a 20% split of the POOLED cohorts and NOT an external cohort. Table 4 (Balanced Accuracy | Macro F1): Cosine similarity (k=3) 0.67 | 0.68; LR (Unbalanced, Uncalibrated) 0.77 | 0.75; LR (Unbalanced, Calibrated) 0.73 | 0.75; LR (Random Oversampling, Uncalibrated) 0.77 | 0.76; LR (Random Oversampling, Calibrated) 0.73 | 0.75; LR (Random Downsampling, Uncalibrated) 0.68 | 0.64; LR (SMOTE, Uncalibrated) 0.78 | 0.76; LR (SMOTE, Calibrated) 0.74 | 0.75. Table 3 (calibrated OvR LR with SMOTE, per class, F1 | Precision | Recall, with test WSI counts): Luminal A n=136 0.84 | 0.79 | 0.89; Luminal B n=53 0.60 | 0.68 | 0.52; HER2 n=39 0.79 | 0.87 | 0.71; Basal n=59 0.80 | 0.78 | 0.81; Macro-average 0.75 | 0.78 | 0.73. Tile-level OvR LR with mean tile-probability aggregation: 'mean balanced accuracy 0.65, mean overall accuracy 0.73 and macro F1 0.68 on the held-out test set (n = 287). Mean precision and recall were 0.76 and 0.65, respectively.' Attention-MIL, calibrated: 'On the held-out test set (n = 287), the model achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.84, overall accuracy of 0.87, macro F1 of 0.83, precision of 0.72, and recall of 0.80.' Table 5 (attention-MIL per class, F1 | Precision | Recall): Luminal A n=136 0.86 | 0.85 | 0.86; Luminal B n=53 0.67 | 0.40 | 0.69; HER2 n=39 0.88 | 0.86 | 0.74; Basal n=59 0.89 | 0.79 | 0.89; Macro-average 0.83 | 0.72 | 0.80. Comparison claim: 'our attention-based MIL approach improves macro F1 score by 10% compared to Masoud Tafavvoghi et al.', their primary benchmark 'because it used the same dataset'. SPLIT TYPE for every number above: a single fixed 80/20 random split with fixed seeds - NOT cross-validation and NOT external. NOTHING IN THIS PAPER IS COMPARABLE TO AN AUROC: the string AUROC appears zero times and AUC appears three times, all as 'ROC-AUC curves' in a metrics list or figure captions, with no numeric AUC value anywhere.
rows.external_validation: NONE - and that is the point of the row. The cohorts are POOLED into one split. Verbatim: 'To ensure fair model selection and evaluation, the dataset was divided into training and test sets using an 80/20 split, with fixed random seeds for reproducibility. Stratified sampling was applied based on both molecular subtype and data source (TCGA, CPTAC, Warwick) to maintain balanced representation across splits.' The training set was further split 8:1:1 into train/validation/calibration. That CPTAC slides consequently appear on BOTH sides of the split is an INFERENCE, not a sentence in the paper - the paper never says so outright. The inference is strong: the test set n=287 is 20.0-20.1% of every class's pooled total (136/678, 53/265, 39/195, 59/295), consistent with one global stratified draw over the pooled set rather than a source-held-out design.
rows.code: A web-based tool is advertised in the abstract ('we provide a web server to support pathology diagnostics'); no repository URL survived the text extraction, so the code location is NR from this retrieval.
rows.caveats: UNREFEREED PREPRINT (bioRxiv, posted 22 December 2025; Europe PMC id PPR1230633, which itself does not resolve to a readable PDF - the working route is paper-search read biorxiv 10.64898/2025.12.19.695372). THE LABEL-MIXING FACT IS CONFIRMED AND IS SERIOUS: Table 1 gives the Warwick 'Labels Source' as IHC while TCGA and CPTAC are PAM50, and all 80 Warwick HER2-positive biopsy slides are counted in the same HER2 column as the expression-derived HER2-enriched cases. Their attention-MIL HER2 F1 of 0.88 is therefore computed on a class that is part PAM50 HER2-enriched and part IHC/FISH HER2-positive - two different biological entities - and it is NOT comparable to a PAM50 HER2-enriched recall. Anyone reading 0.88 as a rebuttal to a 0/14 external Her2 recall would be making exactly that error. Second: no numeric AUROC exists anywhere in the paper, so none of its numbers can be set beside an AUROC. Third: the patient/slide grouping claim is loose - 'For MIL models, all tiles belonging to the same patient (i.e., from the same WSI) were grouped and assigned to a single split, ensuring that no information from a given case was shared between training and evaluation sets' equates a patient with a WSI, so a patient contributing several slides could straddle train and test, and TCGA-BRCA contributes 971 slides for far fewer patients. Fourth: Warwick slides are biopsy specimens with far fewer tiles per slide than resections, which the authors acknowledge as a site-bias risk. HOW TO USE IT: near comparator needing a caveat, whose real job is to ESTABLISH THE NEGATIVE by being the closest published thing to this project that still is not an external validation. It matches on cohort pair (TCGA-BRCA + CPTAC-BRCA), class set (LumA/LumB/HER2/Basal with Normal-like dropped) and backbone (UNI-2, frozen, 1536-dim, 20x, non-overlapping tiles); its TCGA class counts (LumA 502, LumB 221, HER2 76, BL 172) are within a slide or two of this project's manifest (LumA 503, LumB 221, Basal 174, Her2 76), so it is the same data lineage. It then pools the two cohorts into a single 80/20 split stratified by subtype AND source, which is precisely the design this project refuses, and which is why the claim that no published PAM50 model has an external never-trained-on evaluation survives this paper rather than falling to it. Its macro F1 0.83 and balanced accuracy 0.84 are SLIDE-level on a pooled internal split and cannot be set beside a case-level external balanced accuracy.

rows.title: Contrastive Learning for Omics-guided Whole-slide Visual Embedding Representation
rows.authors: Suwan Yu, Yooeun Kim, Hoeyoung Kim (Yu and Kim contributed equally); Sangseon Lee, Kwangsoo Kim (co-corresponding). Seoul National University / Inha University / Seoul National University Hospital. The method is named CLOVER; that acronym is not part of the registered title, which Crossref and the PDF title block both give without it.
rows.venue: bioRxiv preprint, posted 15 January 2025. UNREFEREED - the PDF carries the banner 'which was not certified by peer review' on every page. Europe PMC preprint id PPR966798. No journal venue.
rows.modalities: H&E WSI - the primary modality and the ONLY modality at inference - plus three omics used exclusively as contrastive pretraining targets: RNA-seq, DNA methylation and CNV. Verbatim: 'CLOVER integrates diverse molecular data layers, including genomics (copy number variation), epigenomics (DNA methylation), and transcriptomics (mRNA abundances), to guide the learning of image representations.'
rows.datasets: TCGA-BRCA only. Verbatim: 'The dataset comprises 610 patients, with 658 slides and corresponding multi-omics profiles.' Diagnostic FFPE slides. The PAM50 distribution is stated in SLIDES, verbatim: 'The molecular subtypes showed the following distribution: Luminal A (312), Luminal B (116), Basal-like (112), and HER2-enriched (48) slides' - which sums to 588 of the 658 slides, leaving 70 unaccounted for; patient-level PAM50 counts are NR. Histologic subtypes: IDC 493 slides, ILC 117 slides. Receptor-status slides (positive/negative): HER2 74/308, ER 433/143, PR 433/143. Feature counts after filtering: CNV 7,460 genome-wide segment-level features (segments with under 5% zeros, mean absolute value 0.20 or lower, or coefficient of variation 0.20 or lower removed), RNA-seq 6,016 (log2(TPM+1), SD > 1), methylation 6,617 (probes with beta below 0.3 in more than 90% of samples excluded).
rows.endpoint: Three downstream tasks; the relevant one is 4-class PAM50 molecular subtype, evaluated few-shot and prototype-based. Also binary histologic subtype (IDC vs ILC) and binary ER / PR / HER2 IHC status by linear probing. CLASS COUNT: 4, established three ways - the Methods sentence 'The PAM50 molecular subtype classification system categorizes breast cancer into four subtypes-Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-enriched, and Basal-like'; the Fig. 1 label 'PAM50 Subtypes(LumA/ LumB/ Basal / HER2)'; and the four-way slide distribution 312/116/112/48. Normal-like is absent throughout, matching this project's class set. PREDICTION UNIT: slide. The classification unit is the slide embedding and the PAM50 class counts are stated in slides; a patient-level constraint was applied to the image-omics PAIRING only, verbatim - 'To maintain the integrity of multimodal relationships, we adopted a patient-level approach, preventing improper sampling practices that might associate multiple slides with a single omics profile.' No case-level aggregation of predictions is described. LABEL BASIS: RNA-derived PAM50, curated rather than recomputed - 'We curated metadata from the cBioPortal and GDC portals, including histologic subtype, molecular subtype (based on PAM50 classification), and estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status based on immunohistochemistry (IHC).' The PAM50 CALLER is NR - no mention of nearest-centroid, genefu, Netanely or nCounter anywhere.
rows.wsi_pipeline: Custom patch slicing at 20x, 256x256 px, no overlap; an edge-score filter (threshold 15); plus Hover-Net/PanNuke filtering that excludes patches whose majority cell annotation is 'no-neo' or unlabelled, patches with fewer than five cells, and patches whose major cell-type proportion is below 0.3. Patch encoder = UNI, 1024-dim, N = 2,048 patches per slide. Instance aggregator = ABMIL, mapping to a 786-dim slide embedding (d_hidden = 786).
rows.fusion_method: CONTRASTIVE PRETRAINING ONLY - not fusion at test time. Each omics modality passes through a dedicated two-layer Self-Normalizing Network to a 256-dim embedding; the three are concatenated and projected by a multi-omics aggregator to a 786-dim vector m_i, and a symmetric cross-modal InfoNCE-style contrastive loss aligns the slide embedding h_i with m_i. Downstream, omics are absent: for PAM50, 'we performed prototype-based classification using learned embeddings, where test samples are classified based on their distance to class prototypes constructed from the limited k-shot examples'; for the binary tasks, 'we performed linear probing by fixing the pretrained slide encoder and training a logistic regression classifier on the extracted embeddings.' Fig. 1's downstream panel shows Test Slides -> Patch Embedding -> Instance Aggregator -> Slide Embeddings -> Prototype-based classification, with no omics branch. Abstract: 'CLOVER enables detailed molecular characterization from single slide analysis.'
rows.metrics: PROTOCOL, verbatim: 'we used 5-fold cross-validation with 50 random trials per k-shot scenario (k=1,5,10). For each trial, four folds were used for pretraining and one-fold for testing.' Folds stratified for class balance. Metric wording, verbatim: 'Performance was assessed using AUROC (Area Under ROC Curve) as the primary metric, supplemented by weighted F1-Score and AUPRC' - so the F1 column is a WEIGHTED F1, not macro-F1; the PAM50 narrative calls the AUROC 'macro-AUROC'. All values below are percentages, mean +/- SD, INTERNAL 5-fold CV on TCGA-BRCA, prototype-based, slide level. TABLE 2 (PAM50; F1-score / AUROC / AUPRC): k=1 - UNI+TransMIL 34.9+/-9.7 / 59.2+/-5.6 / 34.0+/-4.9; UNI+ABMIL 35.2+/-10.3 / 60.1+/-5.6 / 34.9+/-5.2; UNI+Avg 31.6+/-11.4 / 58.8+/-5.4 / 33.7+/-4.8; TANGLE 46.6+/-12.8 / 73.8+/-6.3 / 47.8+/-6.6; CLOVER 53.7+/-11.4 / 76.7+/-6.9 / 52.2+/-7.5. k=5 - UNI+TransMIL 49.0+/-6.9 / 69.5+/-5.1 / 43.6+/-5.7; UNI+ABMIL 49.9+/-6.5 / 71.2+/-5.2 / 45.5+/-5.9; UNI+Avg 45.9+/-7.5 / 68.2+/-5.1 / 42.7+/-5.4; TANGLE 65.2+/-4.4 / 84.6+/-3.1 / 60.3+/-5.6; CLOVER 66.0+/-5.0 / 85.8+/-2.9 / 62.3+/-5.5. k=10 - UNI+TransMIL 54.8+/-5.8 / 74.9+/-4.4 / 49.1+/-5.7; UNI+ABMIL 55.9+/-5.5 / 76.6+/-4.3 / 51.3+/-5.8; UNI+Avg 51.0+/-5.8 / 72.5+/-4.5 / 47.3+/-5.2; TANGLE 68.4+/-3.5 / 86.8+/-2.6 / 63.6+/-5.9; CLOVER 68.2+/-3.8 / 87.2+/-2.2 / 64.1+/-5.6. NOTE that at k=10 TANGLE's F1 (68.4) EXCEEDS CLOVER's (68.2), against the narrative's claim of consistent superiority. TABLE 1 (histologic subtype IDC/ILC, same protocol) k=10: CLOVER 85.3+/-5.2 / 89.9+/-4.8 / 75.8+/-10.0; TANGLE 83.8+/-5.0 / 89.7+/-4.5 / 72.6+/-9.2. Clinical markers (AUROC, text): ER 78.1+/-18.3 (k=1) to 86.7+/-5.5 (k=10); PR 68.4+/-19.3 to 76.9+/-6.5; HER2 54.4+/-11.1 to 63.9+/-10.2. SILHOUETTE SCORES, representation evaluation, split type not applicable: 'RNA-seq showed the highest performance for PAM50 classification (silhouette score 0.058), followed by copy number variation (CNV, 0.039) and DNA methylation (0.033)' and 'the integrated multi-omics framework of CLOVER significantly enhanced representation quality, achieving silhouette scores of 0.083 for histologic subtypes, 0.170 for PAM50 classification, and 0.152 for TNBC subtype (Supplementary Figure 1)'. A separate passage in the same section reports 'for PAM50 molecular subtypes, CLOVER demonstrated superior clustering with a silhouette score of 0.089, compared to TANGLE's 0.037'; these two PAM50 silhouettes are most likely two DIFFERENT embeddings rather than an inconsistency - the 0.089 belongs to the slide-embedding comparison in Fig. 2B (where CLOVER's histologic value is 0.112) and the 0.170 to the integrated multi-omics representation in Supplementary Figure 1 (where the histologic value is the lower 0.083). Omics ablation: RNA+MET average rank 2.67 with PAM50 k=10 AUROC 87.2+/-1.8; full RNA+MET+CNV average rank 2.60. Attention correlation with neoplastic cell density rho = 0.89; connective rho = -0.43; inflammatory rho = -0.25.
rows.external_validation: NONE, stated by the authors: 'Several important limitations must be acknowledged. Our evaluation relied solely on TCGA-BRCA data, which may not fully account for image quality variations across different institutions and imaging devices. Also, the lack of external validation across different institutions and patient populations limits our understanding of the model's generalizability.' A scan for the word 'external' across the whole document returns exactly one occurrence - that sentence.
rows.code: NR - no code-availability statement, GitHub URL or data-availability section appears anywhere in the retrieved full text.
rows.caveats: UNREFEREED bioRxiv preprint (Europe PMC PPR966798). Retrieval route: paper-search read biorxiv 10.1101/2025.01.12.632280 by DOI - read europepmc PPR966798 fails with 'does not have an accessible PDF' and search -s biorxiv returns a recency feed rather than the paper. PAM50 class counts are given in SLIDES, not patients, and sum to 588 of 658 slides, so 70 slides are unaccounted for. The CNV representation is 7,460 genome-wide SEGMENT-level features, roughly 190x the 39 arm medians used here, and it is explicitly a pretraining signal only - so this is NOT a WSI+CNV fusion model at inference. TANGLE appears here as an RNA-guided baseline; note that TANGLE itself publishes no PAM50 evaluation, so the PAM50 numbers attributed to TANGLE in this paper are CLOVER's re-implementation and not TANGLE's own published result. The F1 column is a weighted F1 by the paper's own definition and must not be read as macro-F1. HOW TO USE IT: context only - not a fair comparator to any number here, and it does not contest the novelty claim. It DOES resolve the earlier survey's designated highest-value unknown, favourably: 'subtype' here is 4-class PAM50 and CNV is one of three guiding omics, but CNV enters ONLY as a contrastive pretraining target and inference is slide-only, so there is no WSI+CNV fusion at test time, no CNV-alone arm, no fusion operator and no equal-weight-mean baseline. Its 87.2 +/- 2.2 macro-AUROC at k=10 is internal 5-fold TCGA, few-shot, prototype-based and slide-level, and must NOT be set beside an internal case-level 10-fold WSI figure or an external case-level one. Two things it is genuinely useful for: the per-omics silhouette ranking (RNA 0.058 > CNV 0.039 > methylation 0.033) is independent corroboration that CNV alone carries real but sub-RNA PAM50 signal; and it is a second published case of a WSI+omics PAM50 paper with no external cohort, reinforcing the slot this chapter occupies.

rows.title: A deep learning pipeline for PAM50 subtype classification using histopathology images and multi-objective patch selection
rows.authors: Arezoo Borji, Gernot Kronreif, Bernhard Angermayr, Francisco Mario Calisto, Ali Abbasian Ardakani, Wolfgang Birkfellner, Inna Servetnyk, Yinyin Yuan, Sepideh Hatamikia (corresponding). Austrian Center for Medical Innovation and Technology / Danube Private University / Medical University of Vienna / IST Lisbon / MD Anderson.
rows.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.01798, primary category cs.CV. UNREFEREED - no journal venue and no acceptance is claimed. Four versions exist, confirmed from the arXiv submission history: v1 Thu 2 Apr 2026, v2 Sun 19 Apr 2026, v3 Tue 21 Apr 2026, v4 Tue 28 Apr 2026. This row reads v4.
rows.modalities: Unimodal H&E WSI. No genomic, transcriptomic or clinical modality is used as model input, confirmed by the Discussion: 'Unlike prior studies that either lacked external validation, reduced the task to binary classification, or depended on multimodal molecular inputs [15,16,21,22,38,39], our work tackles the complete multi-class PAM50 classification issue ... utilizing only H&E-stained WSIs.'
rows.datasets: TRAIN/INTERNAL: TCGA-BRCA, 627 FFPE WSIs - 'Luminal A (339 slides), Luminal B (131 slides), HER2-enriched (51 slides), and Basal-like (106 slides)' (sums to 627). Split verbatim: 'we performed a slide-level split at the patient-level to prevent data leakage: 80% of patients were used for training and 20% for validation. When multiple WSIs were available for a given patient, all slides were assigned exclusively to the same split.' EXTERNAL: CPTAC-BRCA, '122 H&E-stained FFPE WSIs with subtype annotations, including Luminal A (51 slides), Luminal B (28 slides), HER2-enriched (12 slides), and Basal-like (31 slides)' (sums to 122); 'For CPTAC-BRCA, all 122 WSIs were reserved for external testing.' Provenance is their ref [40] = H. Liu, X. Xie, B. Wang, 'Deep learning infers clinically relevant protein levels and drug response in breast cancer from unannotated pathology images', npj Breast Cancer 10(1):1-11, 2024, doi 10.1038/s41523-024-00620-y.
rows.endpoint: 4-class PAM50 intrinsic subtype (Luminal A / Luminal B / HER2-enriched / Basal-like). CLASS COUNT: 4, from the dataset sentence, from Section 3.7 ('multi-class classification of breast cancer into four PAM50 molecular subtypes') and from the four class rows of Table 1; Normal-like is named in the Introduction as a PAM50 class but is never used. PREDICTION UNIT: CONTRADICTORY, and effectively patch for the reported metrics. Section 3.7 states slide-level aggregation verbatim - 'Slide-level predictions were made by averaging the probabilities, where the per-class probabilities from all selected patches were averaged, and the class with the highest average probability was designated as the final label for the WSI' - but Table 1's only sample-size column is 'Number of patches' (10000 per class on CPTAC; 2097/966/6658/2564 on TCGA) and no slide-count or case-count denominator accompanies any metric. A flexible regex over the whole v4 PDF returns zero hits for 'case-level' and exactly one for 'patient-level', that one being the split sentence. NO case- or patient-level number exists in the paper. LABEL BASIS: MIXED, and unstated for the external cohort. TCGA verbatim: 'For the TCGA-BRCA cohort (N = 627 WSIs), PAM50 subtype labels were obtained from transcriptomic PAM50 results for 426 WSIs, while the remaining 201 WSIs were classified using IHC surrogate markers' - a paragraph that is duplicated in substance across two consecutive paragraphs of the v4 PDF. The authors' own interpretation caveat: 'the findings of this study should be regarded as predicting IHC-aligned intrinsic subtypes, which may not always perfectly align with gene expression-based PAM50 classifications.' The transcriptomic PAM50 caller is NR, and the CPTAC-BRCA label source is NR - the cohort is introduced only as '122 H&E-stained FFPE WSIs with subtype annotations' cited to ref [40], and a scan of all 21 CPTAC occurrences finds no label-provenance sentence.
rows.wsi_pipeline: FFPE slides only. Background cutoff at 20%; blur removal by variance of the Laplacian with patches below 100 discarded; border heuristics; Macenko stain normalization; ImageNet channel normalization. Feature extractor: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-18 with all convolutional layers FROZEN, using the 512-dimensional penultimate embedding. MC-dropout epistemic uncertainty per patch, then NSGA-II multi-objective patch selection over diversity / informativeness / compactness / reliability (population 50, 50 generations, binary tournament size 2, SBX crossover p=0.9, bit-flip mutation p=0.1), run offline per slide before training: 'each WSI yielded a median of approximately 10,000 tissue patches after preprocessing. NSGA-II reduced this to a median of approximately 500 patches per slide, corresponding to an approximate 95% reduction in patch count', at roughly 3 minutes per WSI on a single GPU.
