Classification head on the frozen embeddings: GAP + FC(256, ReLU) + batch norm + dropout 0.5 + softmax; weighted cross-entropy with inverse-frequency class weights; Adam, lr 1e-4, batch 64, max 100 epochs, early stopping on validation accuracy. 'Importantly, the same preprocessing patch selection and processing pipeline was applied to the CPTAC-BRCA cohort.'
rows.fusion_method: None - unimodal. The only aggregation is probability averaging over the selected patches, explicitly contrasted with attention MIL: 'Unlike attention-based multiple instance learning (MIL) methods, which need to determine instance weights from potentially noisy patch collections, probability averaging offers a robust and transparent way to aggregate data when used with curated patch sets.'
rows.metrics: TABLE 1, 'Model performance comparison on internal vs. external test dataset', columns Subtype | Number of patches | Dataset | Precision | Recall | F1-Score | Accuracy | AUC. TCGA-BRCA rows are the internal 20% patient-level held-out split; CPTAC-BRCA rows are the external cohort with no retraining. Basal-like, 2097, TCGA-BRCA: 0.9161 | 0.9008 | 0.9083 | 0.9689 | 0.9907. Basal-like, 10000, CPTAC-BRCA: 0.7738 | 0.8392 | 0.8052 | 0.8392 | 0.9546. HER2-enriched, 966, TCGA-BRCA: 0.9177 | 0.8312 | 0.8723 | 0.9808 | 0.9902. HER2-enriched, 10000, CPTAC-BRCA: 0.8800 | 0.7670 | 0.8196 | 0.7670 | 0.9610. Luminal A, 6658, TCGA-BRCA: 0.9415 | 0.9268 | 0.9341 | 0.929291 | 0.9918 (the accuracy is printed to six decimals in the source). Luminal A, 10000, CPTAC-BRCA: 0.8010 | 0.7569 | 0.7783 | 0.7569 | 0.9426. Luminal B, 2564, TCGA-BRCA: 0.8350 | 0.9099 | 0.8708 | 0.9436 | 0.9831. Luminal B, 10000, CPTAC-BRCA: 0.7591 | 0.8342 | 0.7783 | 0.8342 | 0.9511. Macro Avg, TCGA-BRCA: 0.9026 | 0.8922 | 0.8964 | 0.9114 | 0.9865. Macro Avg, CPTAC-BRCA: 0.8035 | 0.7993 | 0.7995 | 0.7993 | 0.9523. TABLE 2 (ablation, internal only; Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1 | AUC): Full model 0.9114 | 0.9026 | 0.8922 | 0.8964 | 0.9865; No Uncertainty Modeling 0.8732 | 0.8610 | 0.8634 | 0.8660 | 0.9583; No Patch Selection (all patches used) 0.6421 | 0.6315 | 0.6142 | 0.6227 | 0.7912. A 'No Stain Normalization' series appears in the Fig. 6 legend but has NO row in Table 2, and the ablations were single runs by the authors' own admission. THE HEADLINE IS INTERNALLY UNSTABLE WITHIN v4 ITSELF: the arXiv v4 listing abstract reports 'an F1-score of 0.8812 and an AUC of 0.9841 using 627 WSIs from the TCGA-BRCA cohort' and 'an F1-score of 0.7952 and an AUC of 0.9512' externally, and describes 'a custom CNN head', whereas the v4 PDF abstract reports 0.8964 / 0.9865 and 0.7995 / 0.9523 and says 'a fully connected head'. Both are quoted; neither is reconciled.
rows.external_validation: Yes - a genuinely held-out external cohort, never trained on: 'For CPTAC-BRCA, all 122 WSIs were reserved for external testing', with no refitting, thresholding or recalibration on CPTAC described. BUT the evaluation is CLASS-BALANCED and the aggregation unit is contradictory. Table 1's 'Number of patches' column is exactly 10000 for every CPTAC class, against a cohort whose slide composition is LumA 51 / LumB 28 / HER2 12 / Basal 31, so the external metrics are computed on an equalised 10,000-per-class patch set and NOT at natural prevalence. An arithmetic observation about the table, not a claim the authors make: the four CPTAC per-class Recall values 0.8392 / 0.7670 / 0.7569 / 0.8342 have mean 0.799325, which equals both the reported Macro Avg 'Accuracy' 0.7993 and the Macro Avg 'Recall' 0.7993; each CPTAC per-class 'Accuracy' equals its 'Recall' digit for digit; and the four one-vs-rest AUCs 0.9546 / 0.9610 / 0.9426 / 0.9511 average to 0.952275, matching the reported 0.9523. So the external 'Accuracy 0.7993' is a balanced accuracy on a balanced set and the 'AUC 0.9523' is the unweighted mean of four one-vs-rest AUCs. The TCGA rows use a DIFFERENT definition: per-class 'Accuracy' there is one-vs-rest accuracy (0.9689 etc.) and the TCGA Macro Avg Accuracy 0.9114 does not equal the mean of the per-class recalls.
rows.code: NR - no code-availability statement, GitHub URL or data-availability section appears in the v4 full text.
rows.caveats: UNREFEREED arXiv preprint, version v4 (28 April 2026); four versions exist. VERSION DISCREPANCY CONFIRMED AND IT IS WITHIN v4: the arXiv listing abstract and the v4 PDF body disagree on all four headline figures and on the classifier-head description, and the two abstracts differ in their opening sentences entirely. Worse, the 'custom CNN head' wording is NOT merely a metadata artefact - the v4 PDF's own Table 3 row for the Proposed method reads 'NSGA-II-based patch selection + a custom CNN classifier' and Section 3.7 reads 'we trained a CNN-based classification head on the fixed patch embeddings', so the PDF contradicts its own abstract and the metadata agrees with the PDF body against the PDF abstract. The paper also mis-references its own tables: Section 4.2 opens 'As shown in Table 2, after stain normalization, the accuracy of the model was 0.7993 % in CPTAC', but the CPTAC results are in Table 1 and Table 2 is the ablation. The TCGA label-provenance paragraph is duplicated across two consecutive paragraphs. Patient grouping was enforced for the TCGA train/validation split only; nothing patient-level is enforced or reported on CPTAC. The CPTAC slide set (122 WSIs, via the wsi2rppa paper) is a different and much smaller slide set than the 378 slides / 114 cases used here. HOW TO USE IT: near comparator needing a caveat, specifically against the WSI-only external number and NOT against any fusion number. This is the single strongest apparent counterexample to the central novelty claim and it must be handled in text rather than dropped. Why it is not commensurable, in order of weight: (a) their external evaluation is on 10,000 patches PER CLASS, a class-balanced set, whereas this project's is 114 cases at natural prevalence; (b) the reported metrics are indexed by patch counts with no case- or slide-level denominator anywhere, so 0.9523 is NOT established as a case-level number while 0.847 here is; (c) 201 of 627 of their TRAINING labels are IHC surrogates and the CPTAC label basis is never stated, whereas both cohorts here carry RNA-derived PAM50; (d) their CPTAC subset is a different, smaller slide set; (e) the model is unimodal H&E, so it says nothing about fusion, about a CNV-alone arm, or about the equal-weight probability mean. One point the chapter can use rather than merely defend against: their macro-AUC of 0.9523 sits alongside a HER2-enriched recall of 0.7670 on CPTAC, a direct contrast with a WSI arm calling Her2 0/14 - but on a class-balanced patch set with an unstated label basis, so it is evidence about their evaluation design at least as much as about HER2 morphology.

rows.title: Multimodal random subspace for breast cancer molecular subtypes prediction by integrating multi-dimensional data
rows.authors: Fatima-Zahrae Nakach, Ali Idri, Gbegninougbo Aurel Davy Tchokponhoue. The method is named MRSVM (Multimodal Random Subspace Support Vector Machine); the acronym is not part of the registered title, which Crossref returns without it.
rows.venue: Multimedia Tools and Applications, volume 84, pages 32671-32703. Refereed (Springer). Crossref gives published and published-online date-parts [[2024,12,21]]; the Springer page header shows 'Volume 84, pages 32671-32703 (2025) ... Published 21 December 2024', so the online-first year is 2024 and the issue year 2025. Subscription journal, but the full article body was reachable without credentials through the doi.org -> link.springer.com -> idp.springer.com (303) -> link.springer.com?error=cookies_not_supported (302) chain, all HTTP 200.
rows.modalities: FOUR modalities, and BOTH whole-slide images AND copy number variation are among them. Abstract verbatim: 'the Multimodal Random Subspace Support Vector Machine (MRSVM) ensemble that effectively combines multidimensional data encompassing copy number variation, clinical information, gene expression data and histopathological whole slide images to improve the prediction of breast cancer molecular subtypes.' Modality abbreviations used throughout: E = clinical/EHR, G = gene expression, C = copy number variation, H = histopathological.
rows.datasets: TCGA-BRCA only. Verbatim: 'Although the database includes information on 1098 patients, the quantity of available data for each type varies. To ensure consistency, we standardized the dataset size to the number of patients present across all data types, resulting in a final dataset of 1031 patients.' No other cohort. Per-subtype class distribution is NR - a targeted search of the article body found none.
rows.endpoint: FIVE-class breast cancer molecular subtype. Abstract verbatim: '... the MRSVM ensemble based on early fusion achieved the highest accuracy of 88.07% for molecular subtype prediction over the subtypes (Normal-like, Luminal A, Luminal B, HER2-enriched, and Basal-like).' CLASS COUNT: 5, from that explicit class list - which differs from the 4-class setup used here and from the 4 classes in P58 and P59. No output-layer or code evidence was available to corroborate it. PREDICTION UNIT: case-patient, but INFERRED rather than read - the dataset is standardised to 1031 PATIENTS across all four data types, the omics and clinical modalities are inherently per-patient, and the 200 WSI patches per slide are reduced by PCA into a per-patient feature block before fusion; no metric is reported at slide or patch level. No sentence enforcing patient-level splitting exists anywhere in the article, so patient grouping is structural rather than a stated safeguard. LABEL BASIS: NR. The paper never states where the subtype labels for the 1031 patients came from - no PAM50 caller is named and no sentence attributes the labels to TCGA clinical fields, cBioPortal or a computed call; two independent targeted searches of the body returned nothing. The only related sentence is background: 'Immunohistochemistry (IHC) surrogates have facilitated the categorization of breast cancer's molecular subtypes into Luminal A, Luminal B, Her2-enriched, and Basal-like categories' - which lists only FOUR categories and therefore cannot account for the Normal-like class the model predicts. Since Normal-like is a PAM50 class with no IHC surrogate definition, the label set is most likely RNA-derived PAM50, but the paper does not say so and this row records NR rather than inferring.
rows.wsi_pipeline: Patches extracted per WSI, verbatim: 'To ensure visual consistency and to standardize the information contained in the extracted patches, 200 patches in total were extracted from each WSI with various sizes (512x512, 750x750, 1024x1024) corresponding to magnification factors of 20x, 40x, and 60x.' Feature extraction by ResNet50 - 'For the histopathological data, the pre-trained CNN model ResNet50 was employed for classification due to its superior performance compared to other pre-trained CNN models'. Histopathology features are reduced by PCA before bagging. NO stain normalization and NO attention-based MIL, both named by the authors themselves as limitations: 'we did not implement stain normalization techniques to standardize the color variations across different slides' and 'We did not explore the use of attention-based multi-instance learning techniques, which could have helped in learning more robust slide-level representations from histopathology images.'
rows.fusion_method: TWO layers of combination, and neither is a probability mean. (i) Multimodal fusion, verbatim definitions: early fusion is 'Feature-level fusion, encompasses the amalgamation of multiple input modalities into a unified feature vector before their input into a single DL model'; late fusion is 'Decision-level fusion, involves employing predictions from multiple models to make a final decision', using 'separate models trained with different modalities, and an aggregation function combines their predictions'. (ii) The MRSVM ensemble itself combines its members by MAJORITY VOTE: 'The ensemble makes decisions based on a majority vote from a predetermined number of classifiers, each of which is constructed using a distinct, randomly sampled feature subset', with 'each bag represents a random bootstrapped sample of 60% of the training dataset features' and 'each bagging ensemble employs a different number of bags (3, 5, 7 and 9)'. Before bagging, features are dimensionally harmonised per modality, verbatim: 'we utilized Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for quantitative gene expression data and features extracted from histopathological images, and Multiple Correspondence Analysis (MCA) for categorical copy number variation data', plus 'For clinical data, we duplicated the vector of this modality in order to increase its dimensionality to be closer to those of histopathological, or gene features.' The headline finding is that EARLY fusion beat LATE fusion here - the opposite direction to Sucre et al. 2025 (P63).
rows.metrics: Metric set verbatim: 'The evaluation of the performance of the different models constructed was based on the four-performance metrics: accuracy, recall, precision and F1-score.' NO AUC or AUROC is reported anywhere in the paper, confirmed by a targeted full-article query. Split type for every number below: stratified 5-fold cross-validation on TCGA-BRCA - 'A stratified fivefold cross-validation approach was employed' - with no held-out test set and no external cohort. BEST OVERALL, early fusion of gene expression + copy number variation: 'the MRSVM secured the top position with the most favorable outcomes, including an accuracy of 88.07%, a recall of 88.83%, a precision of 82.98%, and an F1-score of 84.62%, this result stemmed from the early fusion of gene expression data and copy number variation data.' SINGLE MODALITIES: gene expression alone 'an accuracy of 86,71%' (comma decimal separator in the original); histopathology alone with ResNet50 'an accuracy of 60.32%, a recall of 42.88%, a precision of 36.86%, and an F1-score of 36.40%'. CNV-alone and clinical-alone accuracies are NR - not extractable as standalone quoted values. BEST LATE FUSION: 'the integration of gene expression data with clinical data achieved the highest accuracy of 87.20%.' Reported optimal modality combinations, verbatim: '(1) gene expression data combined with copy number variation data, (2) all the four modalities combined, and (3) gene expression data combined with clinical data and copy number variation data'. A NUMERIC COLLISION THAT IS NOW RESOLVED AND NEEDS NO FLAG: Borji et al. 2026 (P59) Table 3 attributes '88.07% accuracy, and average AUC of 0.9427 across subtypes' to a DIFFERENT paper, 'T. Liu et al. [54] 2022' (P51 here); since MRSVM reports no AUC at all, the two claims are distinguishable and MRSVM owns its own 88.07%.
rows.external_validation: NONE. Only TCGA-BRCA is used and evaluation is stratified 5-fold cross-validation; a targeted query for an independent cohort returned nothing. The Limitations section (5.8) names three items - no model interpretability assessment, no stain normalization in WSI preprocessing, and no attention-based multi-instance learning - and does NOT name the absence of external validation.
rows.code: NR - no code or data availability URL surfaced in the retrieved article body.
rows.caveats: EVIDENCE CONFIDENCE IS LOWER FOR THIS ROW THAN FOR THE OTHER FULL-TEXT ROWS, and that should be said when citing it. The article body was reached only through the doi.org -> link.springer.com -> idp.springer.com (303) -> link.springer.com?error=cookies_not_supported (302) chain; a direct curl of the DOI with a browser user-agent returned HTTP 302 then 200 but only a 3,038-byte Akamai 'Client Challenge' JavaScript shell with no article content, Semantic Scholar reports openAccessPdf status CLOSED with the abstract elided by the publisher, Crossref and OpenAlex both return a null abstract, and paper-search read openalex W4404039163 refuses outright. Everything quoted above was extracted through WebFetch calls against that final URL and answered by a summarising model rather than read out of a PDF, so every quoted string should be re-verified against the publisher PDF before it is quoted in the thesis. The section headings returned were body-level and consistent across calls, which is why this is recorded as full-text rather than abstract-only. SUBSTANTIVE GAPS THAT REMAIN EVEN WITH THE BODY VISIBLE: the CNV granularity is never stated - gene-level, segment-level or arm-level - the only characterisation being 'The copy number data initially existed as a continuous variable; however, it was adjusted to specific thresholds: -2, -1, 0, 1, 2', which reads as discrete GISTIC-style calls; the CNV feature count is never stated; the subtype label source is never stated; and no per-subtype class distribution is given. Refereed. HOW TO USE IT: context only, but POSITIONING-CRITICAL - this is a genuine third WSI+CNV breast molecular-subtype paper on full-text evidence, so any sentence saying Amer et al. 2025 is the only WSI+CNV PAM50 work is wrong, and wrong twice over given CustOmics (P52). It is nonetheless NOT a fair comparator to any number here: 5 classes including Normal-like against 4; accuracy / recall / precision / F1 only, with no AUROC anywhere, so nothing can be set beside 0.847 / 0.888 / 0.909; internal stratified 5-fold on TCGA-BRCA with no external cohort; and a label basis that is NR, so it cannot even be confirmed that the target is RNA-derived PAM50. On the fusion-operator question it is a WEAK antecedent of an untrained combiner and no more: the ensemble members are combined by MAJORITY VOTE, not by averaging probabilities, which is exactly the distinction the fusion-operator argument turns on. Its headline direction also runs OPPOSITE to Sucre et al. 2025 (early fusion beats late here; late beats early there), worth one sentence as evidence that the early/late verdict in this literature is not stable. Finally, note that its best model (gene expression + CNV, 88.07%) does not contain the WSI modality at all and WSI alone scores 60.32%, so despite being a four-modality paper its result is an omics result and it supplies no evidence that conditioning H&E on copy number helps.

rows.title: Development and validation of a reliable DNA copy-number-based machine learning algorithm (CopyClust) for breast cancer integrative cluster classification
rows.authors: Cameron C. Young, Katherine Eason, Raquel Manzano Garcia, Richard Moulange, Sach Mukherjee, Suet-Feung Chin, Carlos Caldas, Oscar M. Rueda (corresponding). CRUK Cambridge Institute / MRC Biostatistics Unit / Harvard Medical School / DZNE Bonn.
rows.venue: Scientific Reports 14:11861 (2024), published 24 May 2024. Refereed, open access CC-BY 4.0. Crossref, PubMed (PMID 38789621) and PMC11126405 all agree on title, journal and date.
rows.modalities: DNA copy number ONLY. No imaging, and no gene expression at inference. The entire motivation is classification when expression is unavailable: 'Gene expression data is often lacking, and accurate classification of samples into IntClusts with copy number data alone is essential.'
rows.datasets: TRAINING AND INTERNAL VALIDATION: METABRIC, 1980 breast cancer samples, split 80% training / 20% validation, with 'Model performance ... internally validated on 392 (20%) held-out METABRIC samples' and sixteen intra-IntClust outliers removed from the training cohort by local outlier factor. EXTERNAL VALIDATION: TCGA, 1075 samples, scored on TWO different assay platforms - SNP arrays and whole exome sequencing. Verbatim: 'The 1980 breast cancer samples from METABRIC (internal validation) and the 1075 samples from TCGA (external validation) with available copy number and gene expression data were used to train and validate multiclass hyperparameter-optimized XGBoost machine learning algorithms.'
rows.endpoint: 10-class Integrative Cluster (IntClust) subtype, NOT PAM50. Two model designs: 'a 10-class model with the final IntClust label predicted by a single multiclass model and a 6-class model with binary reclassification in which four pairs of IntClusts were combined for initial multiclass classification'; the 6-class-with-binary-reclassification design was selected for final implementation and still emits a 10-way label. CLASS COUNT: 10 (IntClust 1-10), not 4 or 5, and NOT a PAM50 class count. PREDICTION UNIT: case-patient, i.e. one tumour sample; n = 1980 and n = 1075 samples, no slide or patch unit exists. LABEL BASIS: other - Integrative Cluster labels, not PAM50 and not IHC, with two different provenances: 'For METABRIC, IntClust label was assigned from the original manuscript, while for TCGA, label was assigned via the iC10 classifier using copy number and gene expression data.' So the external ground truth is itself an algorithmic call produced by the very classifier CopyClust is benchmarked against.
rows.wsi_pipeline: None - no imaging in this paper.
rows.fusion_method: None - unimodal copy number. The classifier is XGBoost, selected over Random Forest, SVM, LightGBM and Prediction Analysis of Microarrays on overall recall and MCC, with hyperparameters tuned by stratified five-fold cross-validation and random search inside the METABRIC training cohort.
rows.metrics: NO AUROC ANYWHERE, confirmed by exhaustive case-insensitive scan of the full text: 'AUC' 0 hits, 'AUROC' 0 hits, 'c-statistic' 0 hits; the substring 'ROC' returns four hits, three of them inside Proc./Procedia/Proceedings in the reference list and the fourth inside 'Roche' in the competing-interests statement. The metrics are recall, precision, balanced accuracy, specificity, F1 Score and Matthews correlation coefficient, all reported as MICRO-AVERAGES across all IntClusts. FEATURES: 'To reduce noise, a piecewise constant fit (PCF) was applied to the copy number profiles of the METABRIC samples in each IntClust and unique breakpoints across the 10 profiles were identified and converted into 478 genomic regions. The mean copy number in each region was calculated, and these were used as features for XGBoost models' - note the abstract instead says roughly 500 regions. TABLE 2, caption verbatim 'Performance metrics of CopyClust model on TCGA SNP and WES cohorts. Metrics reported as micro-average across all IntClusts', split type = external cohort with the model trained only on METABRIC: TCGA SNP - Recall 0.811, Precision 0.823, Balanced accuracy 0.893, Specificity 0.975, F1 Score 0.811, MCC 0.787. TCGA WES - Recall 0.786, Precision 0.796, Balanced accuracy 0.879, Specificity 0.971, F1 Score 0.786, MCC 0.759. TABLE 1, 'Overall recall of different classifier approaches', footnoted 'Models were applied to TCGA SNP cohort unless otherwise specified' and 'Overall recall is reported as micro-average across all IntClusts', with 95% CIs: Random forest 68.4% (65.5%, 71.1%) MCC 0.651; Support vector machine 68.6% (65.7%, 71.3%) MCC 0.645; LightGBM 71.4% (68.5%, 74.0%) MCC 0.677; Prediction analysis of microarrays 66.8% (63.9%, 69.6%) MCC 0.628; XGBoost - TCGA SNP Cohort 81.1% (78.7%, 83.4%) MCC 0.787; XGBoost - TCGA WES Cohort 78.6% (76.0%, 81.0%) MCC 0.759. Against the current copy-number-only gold standard, quoted as printed: 'Compared to the current gold standard copy number-only iC10 classifier, CopyClust achieved a nine-percentage point greater overall recall when applied to METABRIC (82% vs. 73%) and a 22% and 20% greater overall recall when applied to the TCGA SNP and WES datasets, respectively (81% and 79% vs. 59%)'. Error structure: 'IntClust 3 and IntClust 8 were the most misclassified pair of IntClusts, likely due to their similar copy number profiles. IntClust 6 experienced the lowest individual recall'.
rows.external_validation: YES - a genuine cross-cohort AND cross-platform external validation, never pooled into training: 'Model performance was internally validated on 392 (20%) held-out METABRIC samples and externally validated on the TCGA dataset, with copy number data generated from both single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) arrays and whole exome sequencing (WES)'. One caveat the authors state themselves: 'Scaling of feature values was performed prior to model implementation on external cohorts', and 'the need to apply feature scaling across samples limits performance when there are only a single or few samples to classify' - so a per-cohort feature scaling step IS applied to the external data, a mild but real form of touching the external set. They also flag: 'CopyClust was only trained using a single cohort and validated externally on a single cohort, therefore, replication on additional datasets may further improve performance.'
rows.code: https://github.com/camyoung54/CopyClust - 'The underlying code for this study is available in GitHub and can be accessed via this link'. Data: METABRIC and TCGA via cBioPortal (brca_metabric, brca_tcga).
rows.caveats: THE SENTENCE THIS PAPER IS OFTEN EXPECTED TO CONTAIN IS NOT IN IT. There is no statement anywhere in the body that the algorithm does not predict PAM50 intrinsic subtypes; an exhaustive scan returns exactly ONE occurrence of PAM50, and it is Introduction background - 'A classifier system called PAM50 was later derived to assign one of these groups to any tumor based on its expression profile.' If such a disclaimer exists it is in the Supplemental Methods, which were not retrieved. THE POINT STILL STANDS but must be made from the design rather than from a quote: the target is IntClust throughout, PAM50 appears once and only as history, and the stated motivation is IntClust assignment for samples lacking expression data. So this paper establishes the negative by omission - nobody has done copy-number-only classification for PAM50 - not by an explicit disclaimer. Second caveat: the external TCGA IntClust LABELS were themselves generated by the iC10 classifier from copy number AND gene expression, so the external ground truth is an algorithmic call and the comparator iC10 is the same algorithm that produced the labels. Third: no AUROC anywhere, so nothing here can be compared to any AUROC. Fourth: no sWGS, low-pass, coverage or cost claim is made anywhere - scans for 'shallow', 'sWGS', 'low-pass' and 'cost' all return zero hits, and the assays are SNP array and WES. Fifth: the genomic SCALE of the 478 regions is never stated in base pairs or relative to chromosome arms, and the substring 'arm' returns zero hits in the whole paper; the only spatial statement is 'Manual curation of genomic ranges developed from PCF was only performed to ensure that ranges did not span multiple chromosomes but ranges still cover regions of telomeres and centromeres.' Refereed. HOW TO USE IT: context only, and load-bearing context for two separate claims. It is NOT a numeric comparator - 10-class IntClust rather than 4-class PAM50, and no AUROC anywhere - so it cannot be set against a CNV-alone 0.888 external or 0.866 internal. What it buys: (1) it is the strongest published evidence that a copy-number-ONLY breast classifier transports across cohorts AND across assay platforms - METABRIC-trained, TCGA-tested on SNP array (recall 81.1%, balanced accuracy 0.893) and on WES (78.6%, 0.879) - which is the cross-platform robustness a TCGA-SNP6-to-CPTAC-WGS transfer depends on, and the per-arm r = 0.960 platform-correlation control here is the analogous check; (2) it establishes the negative cleanly, since the best-executed copy-number-only breast taxonomy classifier in the literature targets IntClust and not PAM50. On feature coarseness it is a WEAK support for a 39-arm choice rather than a strong one: 478 piecewise-constant-fit regions is roughly twelve times that feature count, derived from array and exome data with no sWGS or cost claim anywhere, so it shows that a few hundred copy-number regions suffice for a 10-class breast taxonomy, not that arm scale does.

rows.title: Genomic copy number predicts esophageal cancer years before transformation
rows.authors: Sarah Killcoyne and Eleanor Gregson (joint first), David C. Wedge, Dan J. Woodcock, Matthew Eldridge, Rachel de la Rue, Ahmad Miremadi, Sujath Abbas, Adrienn Blasko, Cassandra Kosmidou, Wladyslaw Januszewicz, Aikaterini Varanou Jenkins, Moritz Gerstung et al., Rebecca C. Fitzgerald (corresponding, MRC Cancer Unit, University of Cambridge)
rows.venue: Nature Medicine 26, 1726-1732 (2020). Refereed. Crossref and PubMed (PMID 32895572) agree; the text read here is the Europe PMC Funders author manuscript, PMC7116403.
rows.modalities: Genomic copy number ONLY, from shallow whole-genome sequencing of FFPE endoscopic biopsies. No imaging modality in the model - p53 immunohistochemistry and histopathology are used as clinical comparators and for endpoint definition, not as model inputs.
rows.datasets: THREE cohorts. DISCOVERY: a nested, demographically matched case-control cohort - 'shallow whole genome sequencing (sWGS; average depth 0.4x) in a retrospective, demographically matched, case-control cohort of patients (n=88) with all available endoscopy samples (n=777) collected during clinical surveillance for BE', over a period of up to 15 years; 'A total of 777 samples were sequenced with 773 passing our post-processing quality control'. VALIDATION 1: 'an independent cohort of 76 patients (n=213 samples)', of which 'A total of 219 samples were sequenced from this cohort, with 213 passing our post-processing quality control'. VALIDATION 2, orthogonal and on a different assay: the historical Seattle BE Study SNP array cohort, 248 patients. Non-dysplastic BE samples n=518 in the discovery cohort.
rows.endpoint: Risk of PROGRESSION, with the model endpoint being high-grade dysplasia or intramucosal cancer: 'a cross-validated elastic-net regularized logistic regression model of progression and classification with the endpoint HGD or intramucosal cancer (IMC; Methods)'. NO molecular subtype endpoint of any kind exists in this paper - scans for 'subtype' and 'PAM50' both return zero hits across the entire full text. CLASS COUNT: 2 (progressor vs non-progressor); predictions are subsequently discretised into three RISK CLASSES (low / moderate / high) by thresholding the binary probability at 0.3 and 0.5, but those are risk strata, not classes of a multiclass model. PREDICTION UNIT: sample, i.e. an individual endoscopic biopsy, with patient-level and endoscopy-level aggregation tested and found not to help: 'Aggregating predictions either per-endoscopy (mean or max sample predictions) or per-patient (mean or max predictions excluding HGD/IMC samples) did not measurably increase the prognostic accuracy (Supplementary Fig. 2b), suggesting that a single sample (e.g. pooled 4-quadrant biopsy) may be sufficient for prediction'. Cross-validation folds were drawn per-patient, so patient grouping was enforced. LABEL BASIS: other - a histopathological progression outcome, not a molecular subtype. Cases are patients who progressed to HGD/IMC during surveillance; controls are demographically matched non-progressors, matched for age, gender, BE segment length and smoking status.
rows.wsi_pipeline: None. Tissue is processed 'from scrolls, without microdissection'; an additional section at each level of the Barrett's segment (n=88 patients, n=590 sections) underwent p53 IHC, used as a clinical comparator rather than a model input.
rows.fusion_method: None - unimodal copy number.
rows.metrics: THE COPY-NUMBER REPRESENTATION IS THE REASON THIS ROW EXISTS, Methods verbatim: 'We encoded all CN data on a genome-wide scale by taking a weighted average of the segmented values per 5Mb windows, and mean standardization per genomic window. In order to evaluate chromosomal instability on a larger scale we averaged the segmented values across chromosome arms and adjusted each 5Mb window by the difference between the window and the arm. The resulting data was 589 5Mb windows and 44 chromosome arms. We additionally included a measure of genomic complexity (cx) by summing, per-sample, the 5Mb windows that had CN values two standard deviations from the mean.' Upstream: 'pre-processing of the reads for mappability, GC content, and filtering was performed with QDNAseq using 50kb bins ... Samples were segmented for CN analysis using the piecewise constant fit function (pcf) in the R Bioconductor copynumber v1.16 package.' Sequencing: 'Single-end 50-base pair sequencing was performed at a depth of 0.4X on the Illumina HiSeq platform.' MODEL: elastic-net regularised logistic regression via R glmnet, tuned on QDNAseq bin size and elastic-net penalty; 'For the regression penalty parameter, all models had a cross-validation classification rate of 72-75%. We therefore selected the parameter that limited the number of coefficients (n=74) and was not full lasso (e.g. 0.9).' SPLIT TYPE: '5-fold cross validation repeated 10 times was performed on a per-patient basis removing all samples from 20% of patients in each fold', with overall accuracy estimated by 'a leave-one-patient out analysis (excluding all samples of an individual) ... using the area under the ROC curve using the R pROC package'. THE ONLY AUC VALUE IN THE MAIN TEXT, verbatim: 'With each increment in the number of patients the predictive accuracy of the model increased, reaching a (cross validated) AUC of 0.89 (specificity=0.83, sensitivity=0.82) when combining all discovery and validation patients (n=164; Supplementary Fig. 6)' - a sub-sampling learning-curve endpoint over discovery and validation POOLED, NOT a clean independent-cohort AUC. A scan for AUC across the full text returns exactly three occurrences, and this is the only one carrying a value; no confidence interval accompanies any discrimination metric anywhere. RISK CLASS CALIBRATION: 'low' (Pr<=0.3; sensitivity=0.87, specificity=0.65), 'moderate' (0.3>Pr<0.5), 'high' (Pr>=0.5, sensitivity=0.72, specificity=0.82) - the malformed moderate interval is in the source. DISCOVERY CLASSIFICATION: 'CN profiles in NDBE samples that belonged to progressor patients were classified as high risk in 60.5% (104/172) while in non-progressor patients 64.7% (224/346) of samples were classified as low risk.' VALIDATION COHORT (76 patients, 213 samples): '78/142 (55%) samples from non-progressor patients were classified as low risk, and 55/71 (77%) of samples from patients who progressed were classified as high risk.' SEATTLE COHORT: no metric value is given - only 'we again find that samples from progressors are classified as high risk regardless of pathology' and 'in this case the algorithm unsurprisingly suffers a loss of accuracy due to the differences in the methodology'. LEAD TIME: 'For patients that progress, 50% (8/16) of endoscopies had at least one sample classified as high risk 8 or more years prior to transformation' and 'leading to 78% (18/23) of endoscopies with at least one high risk sample one to two years prior to HGD/IMC diagnosis.'
rows.external_validation: YES, two independent cohorts, neither pooled into training for the primary analysis: 'a cross-validated elastic-net regularized logistic regression model of progression ... subsequently validated using an independent cohort of 76 patients (n=213 samples), alongside an orthogonal validation of the Seattle BE Study SNP array samples (n=1272)'. IMPORTANT QUALIFICATION: the one AUC figure quoted (0.89) is explicitly from a sub-sampling analysis 'when combining all discovery and validation patients (n=164)', i.e. discovery and validation POOLED, so it is not an independent-cohort discrimination estimate; no AUC is reported for either validation cohort separately. The Seattle validation used a different assay (SNP array, not sWGS) and the authors note a loss of accuracy 'due to the differences in the methodology'.
rows.code: https://github.com/gerstung-lab/BarrettsProgressionRisk - 'The code and model that support these findings have been provided as an R package in a GitHub repository'. Sequencing data at EGA accession EGAD00001006033.
rows.caveats: Refereed (Nature Medicine), but read via the Europe PMC Funders AUTHOR MANUSCRIPT (PMC7116403), not the typeset version of record, so table and figure numbering may differ and supplementary numbers were not retrieved. TWO INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES, reported and not reconciled. (a) The Seattle cohort sample count is given as n=1272 in the Results paragraph introducing the validations and as samples=1273 a few paragraphs later; each string occurs exactly once. (b) The second validation cohort size is given as 'An independent unmatched cohort of 75 patients was subsequently selected' in the Methods, immediately followed by a breakdown of 18 progressors plus 58 non-progressors = 76, against the Summary and Results figure of 76. THE ABSTRACT CARRIES NO PERFORMANCE FIGURE AT ALL, and even in the full text there is only ONE AUC value, it is pooled across discovery and validation, and no CI accompanies any discrimination metric. NO COST FIGURE OR SEQUENCING BUDGET is stated anywhere despite the low-cost claim - 'cost' occurs exactly twice, in 'These methods are low cost and applicable to standard clinical biopsy samples' and 'the combined use of low-cost genomic technologies, standard clinical samples and statistical modelling', and 'price' returns zero hits; the only quantitative proxy for cheapness is the sequencing configuration itself (single-end 50 bp, 0.4x, Illumina HiSeq). WRONG ORGAN AND WRONG ENDPOINT - oesophagus, progression risk, no molecular subtype anywhere - so this is precedent for the ASSAY CLASS only. Note also a substantial QC attrition on the method-development sample set ('This excluded more than 73% (171/233) from the quality control samples across all sample types'), though only 0.5% and 2% were excluded in the discovery and validation cohorts. HOW TO USE IT: context only - the flagship precedent for the assay class a CNV arm assumes, and irrelevant as a number. What it buys, precisely, is the strongest published evidence that a shallow-WGS copy-number classifier is clinically constructible and clinically validated on standard biopsy material AND - more specifically than expected - that ARM-SCALE features are part of such a model, since the encoding is stated verbatim as '589 5Mb windows and 44 chromosome arms'. That is a direct, citable precedent that chromosome-arm-level copy number is a legitimate feature scale for a low-pass WGS classifier, which is exactly the design justification for 39 arm medians. Two limits on how hard to lean: the model is NOT arm-only (589 5Mb windows dominate the feature count, plus one genomic-complexity scalar, with 74 non-zero coefficients retained), so it supports 'arm-scale features are usable at 0.4x' and not 'arm-scale alone suffices'; and the low-cost claim is qualitative with no cost figure attached. The endpoint distinction - progression risk, not molecular subtype - must be drawn explicitly rather than left for the reader to infer.

rows.title: Multimodal fusion strategies for survival prediction in breast cancer: A comparative deep learning study
rows.authors: Aurora Sucre, Xabier Calle Sanchez, Laura Valeria Perez-Herrera, Maria dM Vivanco, Maria Jesus Garcia-Gonzalez, Karen Lopez-Linares, Borja Calvo, Alba Garin-Muga (Crossref author order; Vicomtech / UPV-EHU affiliations)
rows.venue: Computational and Structural Biotechnology Journal, volume 27 (2025), pages 4505-4516. Refereed, open access. IDENTITY CONFIRMED OUT OF BAND: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.csbj.2025.10.038 currently returns HTTP 403 because the DOI now redirects to spj.science.org (CSBJ has migrated to Science Partner Journals hosting) and that host blocks automated requests; the record was confirmed via the Crossref API and the Europe PMC full text, whose running footer reads 'Computational and Structural Biotechnology Journal 27 (2025) 4505-4516'.
rows.modalities: SIX data sources in three groups: clinical (CL, 27 features), omics (OM = somatic SNV, RNA expression, gene-level CNV, miRNA expression), and imaging (IM = H&E whole-slide images). Abstract verbatim: 'We integrated clinical variables, somatic mutations, RNA expression, copy number variation, miRNA expression, and histopathology images from The Cancer Genome Atlas breast cancer dataset.'
rows.datasets: TCGA-BRCA only. Table 1 per-modality patient and feature counts (PATIENTS | FEATURES | TRAIN | VAL | TEST): Clinical 1084 | 27 | 728 | 181 | 175; Somatic SNV 967 | 1874 | 634 | 158 | 175; RNA Expression 1093 | 4863 | 735 | 183 | 175; Gene-Level CNV 1035 | 4868 | 688 | 172 | 175; miRNA Expression 1076 | 981 | 721 | 180 | 175; Imaging 872 | - | 558 | 139 | 175. Integrated sets: OM (L) 735, OM+CL (L) 726, OM+IM (L) 675, CL+IM (L) 861, OM+CL+IM (L) 666; OM (E) 735 with 12,586 features, OM+CL (E) 726 with 12,613, OM+CL+IM (E) 666 with 13,636. Only primary tumour samples from female patients were kept.
rows.endpoint: Overall survival, discretised into survival categories and scored by concordance index and Integrated Brier Score. NO subtype task exists - PAM50 appears only as an INPUT clinical feature, verbatim: 'The chosen clinical features consisted of patient-level variables extracted from TCGA, including demographic data (age at index; age of diagnosis; and race), tumor subtype (PAM50, OncoTree), and pathological features (stage). Preprocessing included one-hot encoding of categorical variables (race, OncoTree and PAM50)'. CLASS COUNT: NR and not applicable - the late-integration input dimensionality in Table 1 is (number of modalities) x 4, which indicates FOUR discrete survival intervals in the output layer, but that is a time discretisation and not a class count in the subtype sense; no PAM50 class count is predicted anywhere. PREDICTION UNIT: case-patient throughout - every count in Table 1 is patients, the fixed test set is 175 patients, and WSI features are aggregated to the patient by attention-based MIL before fusion; no slide-level or patch-level metric is reported. LABEL BASIS: other - overall survival outcome from TCGA clinical data, discretised into intervals. Not a subtype label.
rows.wsi_pipeline: 'They were processed using the CLAM pipeline for automated tissue segmentation followed by 512 x 512 patch extraction. Each extracted patch was encoded into a 1024-dimensional feature vector using pretrained deep neural networks.' Two encoders were compared, named in Section 2.2.3 - 'The MIL framework included a feature extractor where two encoders were tested: ResNet-50 general-purpose model [17], and UNI pathology foundation model [18]' - and the selection is stated one section later without naming the model: 'The general-purpose encoder produced the best test results (0.649 +/- 0.034) and was thus chosen for integration.' So ResNet-50 was chosen over UNI by a two-sentence chain; UNI's own C-index is NR, deferred to Supplementary SM3. Attention-based MIL for slide-level aggregation, then a fully connected layer to predict survival categories.
rows.fusion_method: NOT a probability mean - a LEARNED STACKER over logits. Verbatim: 'Early integration involved concatenating feature matrices from the four omics types into a single input vector for model training. Conversely, late integration used the optimized unimodal models to generate output logits (unnormalized scores from the last model layer), which were concatenated and passed to a secondary fusion network.' Table 1 corroborates the stacker input dimensionality as (number of modalities) x 4 survival intervals: OM (L) '4 x 4 = 16', OM+CL (L) '5 x 4 = 20', OM+IM (L) '5 x 4 = 20', CL+IM (L) '2 x 4 = 8', OM+CL+IM (L) '6 x 4 = 24'. Loss: negative log-likelihood based on the PORPOISE methodology.
rows.metrics: METRIC AND SPLIT TYPE, verbatim: 'The performance of all models was evaluated using the C-Index (discrimination) and the IBS (calibration). Results are presented as the mean +/- Standard Deviation (SD) of the 5-fold cross-validation runs (Table 3)', with the Test column computed on a FIXED held-out set - 'we defined a fixed test set comprising 175 patients, corresponding to 20 % of the smallest unimodal dataset. This test set was held out for final performance assessment and was not used during training or hyperparameter tuning' - and 'All metrics were computed as five independent values generated by the 5-fold cross-validation scheme (one value per fold).' AN INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY, REPORTED BOTH WAYS AND NOT RECONCILED: Table 3 gives MCAT test 0.658+/-0.051 and MGCT test 0.552+/-0.016, while Section 3.3.1 states 'all three demonstrated high training performance (mean C-indices > 0.936) but exhibited limited out-of-sample generalization with a significant decrease in testing performance (MCAT: 0.685 +/- 0.051; PORPOISE: 0.546 +/- 0.014; MGCT: 0.543 +/- 0.012)'. PORPOISE agrees in both places; MCAT differs in the mean and MGCT differs in both mean and SD. Cite the source passage whenever either figure is used, and do not average them.
rows.external_validation: NONE, and the authors say so explicitly with their reasons. Section 4.4.3, verbatim: 'we recognize that external validation would substantially strengthen this study; however, pursuing this goal was restricted by critical constraints associated with alternative public datasets that were identified for this matter: METABRIC and CPTAC. - The METABRIC cohort was discarded due to differences in the quantification and technological platforms used for several data types, preventing a fair and consistent evaluation against our TCGA-trained models. - The CPTAC initiative is a proteomic extension of the TCGA project and could not be considered an independent dataset for true external validation, as it utilizes a subset of the same patient samples.' The held-out 175-patient test set is an INTERNAL hold-out from TCGA, not an external cohort.
rows.code: https://github.com/amsucre/brca-survival, plus a translational web application at https://brca-model.vicomtech.org. Data from TCGA via the GDC data portal and UCSC Xena.
rows.caveats: Refereed (CSBJ). ACCESS NOTE: the DOI returns HTTP 403 via spj.science.org, and both paper-search read europepmc PMC12595345 and read pmc PMC12595345 fail; the working route is by PMID, paper-search read europepmc PMID:41209345. THE TABLE-VERSUS-TEXT INCONSISTENCY IS REAL and must travel with any quotation of the MCAT or MGCT figures. ONE FACTUAL CLAIM IN THIS PAPER DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS THIS PROJECT'S SETUP AND IS WORTH A SENTENCE: they dismiss CPTAC as an external cohort on the grounds that 'it utilizes a subset of the same patient samples' as TCGA. That is quoted above as their stated reason; it is not a characterisation of CPTAC-BRCA this project accepts, since the CPTAC-BRCA cohort used here is an independent 114-case set with its own accrual. Flagged as a claim to contest, not as an established fact. Other caveats: the endpoint is survival, so NOTHING here is a numeric comparator for any subtype result; PAM50 enters only as an input feature; the CNV arm is 4,868 GENE-LEVEL features - roughly 125x 39 arm medians - filtered to cancer-related genes by the CGN MSigDB gene set, which is a biologically supervised filter and therefore a different kind of feature set from unsupervised arm medians; and the 'Ref' column reproduces each benchmark's originally published C-index (MCAT 0.580, PORPOISE 0.628, MGCT 0.608), which their own re-runs do not reproduce in either direction. HOW TO USE IT: context only - it corroborates the MECHANISM and never the number, and one detail actually weakens the corroboration one might want. It is the closest published design on the modality side (TCGA-BRCA, H&E WSI plus gene-level CNV among six modalities, one protocol, three re-run benchmarks) and its headline direction matches: separately trained modality-specific models combined afterwards beat both feature concatenation and three published joint architectures, verbatim 'In conclusion, the performance hierarchy of this study advocates for simpler frameworks that prioritize modality-specific learning before the final fusion step.' Their re-run of MCAT, PORPOISE and MGCT collapsing from training C-indices above 0.936 to test C-indices of 0.658/0.546/0.552 is an independent instance of published joint operators failing to generalise, and they say so: 'the poor out-of-sample generalization of the established late and intermediate benchmark models (MCAT, PORPOISE, MGCT), exhibited by its significant performance drop from training to testing, justifies the need for the optimized and highly stable architectures developed in this study.' BUT their 'late integration' is NOT an equal-weight probability mean - it concatenates the unimodal models' output LOGITS and passes them to a secondary fusion network, i.e. a LEARNED stacker, which in this project's vocabulary is closer to the stacking arm than to the untrained mean, and the stacker here did not beat the mean either. So this paper corroborates 'train the modalities separately' and does NOT corroborate 'the untrained average beats trained operators'; the text must say which of the two claims it supports. Two further usable points: their CNV-alone arm is the WORST omics modality (test C-index 0.49 +/- 0.031, at chance), a striking contrast with a CNV arm being the stronger unimodal arm externally here, best explained by endpoint - copy number predicts subtype far better than it predicts survival, which is itself an argument for the endpoint chosen here over the parked survival thread; and their imaging arm at 0.546 +/- 0.014 with ResNet-50 chosen over UNI is a reminder that encoder choice is endpoint-dependent.

rows.title: Real-world benchmarking and validation of foundation model transformers for endometrial cancer subtyping from histopathology
rows.authors: Vincent M. Wagner, Casey M. Cosgrove, Stephanie J. Chen, Daniel T. Griffin, Megan I. Samuelson, Michael J. Goodheart, Jesus Gonzalez-Bosquet
rows.venue: npj Precision Oncology (2026) 10:198. Refereed, published in partnership with The Hormel Institute, University of Minnesota. Crossref and the retrieved full text's running header and citation footer agree.
rows.modalities: Unimodal H&E WSI. No genomic modality is a model input; molecular data supply the ground-truth labels only.
rows.datasets: TWO cohorts, and the structure must NOT be misread as a TCGA-to-CPTAC transfer. PUBLIC DISCOVERY COHORT = TCGA AND CPTAC POOLED, verbatim: 'WSIs and matched molecular data were obtained from TCGA and CPTAC; TCGA-UCEC (n = 523), TCGA-UCS (n = 52), and CPTAC-UCEC (n = 240) projects ... After compiling, 815 unique patients were identified. These individuals contributed 1195 diagnostic H&E WSIs (median 1 slide per patient, IQR 1-2).' EXTERNAL COHORT = a third, real-world institution: 'An independent cohort was assembled under IRB approval ... The cohort included 720 patients with endometrial cancer between 2014 and 2017, yielding 1357 WSIs with confirmed molecular labels ... No slides or patients from this cohort were used during model development; they were reserved exclusively for held-out deployment testing.' TABLE 1 (Subtype | TCGA+CPTAC Patients, Slides | External Patients, Slides | Total Patients, Slides): p53abn 246, 325 | 67, 154 | 313, 479. NSMP 272, 454 | 480, 866 | 752, 1320. dMMR 234, 335 | 160, 294 | 394, 629. POLE 63, 81 | 13, 43 | 76, 124. Total 815, 1195 | 720, 1357 | 1535, 2552.
rows.endpoint: 4-class endometrial cancer molecular classification: MMR-deficient (dMMR), p53 aberrant (p53abn), POLE pathogenic mutation (POLE), and no specific molecular profile (NSMP). Wrong organ for this project - endometrium, not breast - so it is precedent for the failure mode only. CLASS COUNT: 4, from the abstract's explicit class list, from the pipeline sentence ('a classifier that produces probabilistic predictions for the four molecular subtypes (p53abn, NSMP, dMMR, and POLE)') and from Table 1's four subtype rows. PREDICTION UNIT: slide - 'Tile-level outputs or embeddings are then aggregated into a slide-level representation using simple mean pooling (CNN pipeline) or attention-based MIL approaches, including TransMIL or CLAM', and 'five-fold cross-validation was performed with slide-level splitting'; Table 1 reports both patients and slides but the modelling unit is the slide. LABEL BASIS: other, i.e. endometrial molecular classification and not PAM50. Discovery labels verbatim: 'Molecular ground-truth labels were derived from molecular annotations on each platform and mapped to their corresponding clinical surrogate categories (p53abn, NSMP, dMMR, POLE) to ensure consistency with the external validation cohort.' External labels verbatim: 'Molecular subtype was determined using IHC for MMR and NGS for TP53 and POLE (only known pathogenic mutations were labeled positive).'
rows.wsi_pipeline: Modified HIA + STAMP pipeline with no manual annotation and no tumour segmentation. STAIN NORMALIZATION DELIBERATELY OMITTED, verbatim: 'Stain normalization was intentionally omitted, as recent work has shown that color normalization may impair generalization of foundation models by altering biologically meaningful stain-morphology correlations learned during large-scale pretraining.' Tiles fixed at a physical field of view: '256 x 256 um of tissue and were extracted as 224 x 224 pixel images after rescaling each WSI to a target MPP of approximately 1.14 um/pixel'. Two tile-level QC steps: a brightness filter (mean grayscale >= 240 excluded) and a Canny edge-density filter (thresholds 40-100, tiles below 2% edge density excluded); 'Across slides, a median of 44% of tiles were filtered (IQR 37-52%)'. Encoders, all frozen: ViT-B/16 baseline, CTransPath, Prov-GigaPath, H-Optimus-0, UNI-2, Virchow2, plus four end-to-end CNNs (EfficientNet-B7, ResNet-18, ResNet-50, DenseNet, freeze ratio 0.5). Aggregators: TransMIL and CLAM; the CNN pipeline aggregates by mean pooling of tile outputs.
rows.fusion_method: None - unimodal. The comparison axis is encoder x aggregator, not modality fusion.
rows.metrics: PRIMARY METRIC AND SPLIT TYPES, verbatim: 'The primary outcome metric was the unweighted mean of the per-subtype AUC (macro-AUC) ... Secondary metrics included macro-F1 score ... and balanced accuracy (the mean recall across subtypes)'. Internal = five-fold cross-validation with SLIDE-LEVEL splitting on the pooled TCGA+CPTAC discovery cohort. External = 'each of the five models trained during cross-validation was applied without retraining to the independent external cohort. Performance metrics reported for external validation therefore represent the distribution of results obtained by applying these five independently trained models to the same held-out real-world dataset', with 'Performance metrics ... reported as means with 95% confidence intervals (95%CI) calculated across the five models' and comparisons by two-sided paired t-tests on fold-level metric vectors with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. INTERNAL: 'foundation encoder models outperformed CNNs (macro-AUC 0.799-0.860 vs 0.715-0.829)'; best configuration Virchow2 with CLAM - 'a macro-AUC of 0.860 (95%CI 0.839-0.880), macro-F1 of 0.607 (95%CI 0.565-0.648,) and a balanced accuracy of 0.647 (95%CI 0.623-0.670)' (the stray comma is in the source). EXTERNAL: 'All CNNs experienced pronounced degradation in performance when compared to cross-validation: EfficientNet, DenseNet, and both ResNets fell to macro-AUC of 0.528-0.588, macro-F1 below 0.252, and balanced accuracy less than 0.286'; the baseline ViT reached macro-AUC 0.626; foundation encoders with TransMIL produced 'macro-AUCs from 0.712-0.761, macro-F1s from 0.311 to 0.424, and balanced accuracies from 0.433-0.519'; 'Prov-GigaPath with CLAM outperformed Prov-GigaPath with TransMIL by 0.046 macro-AUC points (0.777 vs 0.731) and achieved the highest macro-F1 of any model (0.438, 95%CI 0.402-0.474)'; 'UNI2 with CLAM yielded the top macro-AUC overall (0.780, 95%CI 0.750-0.810) with macro-F1 0.416 (95%CI 0.339-0.493) and balanced accuracy 0.507 (95%CI 0.445-0.570)'. Sensitivity analysis: 'macro-AUC excluding POLE = 0.794, 95%CI 0.778-0.810'. PER-SUBTYPE AUCs, INTERNAL: UNI2+CLAM p53abn 0.942 (0.933-0.951) and dMMR 0.792 (0.757-0.827); Virchow2+CLAM NSMP 0.869 (0.847-0.891); Virchow2+TransMIL POLE 0.849 (0.810-0.888). PER-SUBTYPE AUCs, EXTERNAL: UNI2+CLAM p53abn 0.851 (0.837-0.865), NSMP 0.770 (0.746-0.794), dMMR 0.759 (0.718-0.800); Virchow2+TransMIL POLE 0.798 (0.752-0.844). PER-CLASS EXTERNAL RECALLS from the normalized confusion matrix of UNI2+CLAM, verbatim: 'NSMP tumors showed the highest classification fidelity (per-class recall of 0.72), followed by p53abn (0.63) and POLE (0.54), while dMMR showed low recall (0.14).'
rows.external_validation: YES - a genuine, never-trained-on external cohort at a third real-world institution, applied without retraining: 'No slides or patients from this cohort were used during model development; they were reserved exclusively for held-out deployment testing to evaluate generalization performance of the models from cross-validation.' External labels were determined independently by IHC for MMR and NGS for TP53 and POLE.
rows.code: Partial. 'STAMP (https://github.com/KatherLab/STAMP), HIA (https://github.com/KatherLab/HIA), CLAM (https://github.com/mahmoodlab/CLAM), Custom scripts used for preprocessing, experiment orchestration, and evaluation in this study will be publicly available at the time of publication at: https://github.com/wagnerlabuiowa/ec-subtyping-benchmark'. Institutional slides cannot be shared (HIPAA/IRB); de-identified derivatives may be shared on request.
rows.caveats: Refereed (npj Precision Oncology). WRONG ORGAN - endometrium, not breast - so this is precedent for the FAILURE MODE and never a comparator number. COHORT STRUCTURE MUST NOT BE MISREAD: the discovery set POOLS TCGA and CPTAC (815 patients / 1195 WSIs), so this is NOT a TCGA-to-CPTAC transfer; the external set is a third institution's real-world cohort (720 patients / 1357 WSIs, 2014-2017). NO PRIOR CORRECTION, THRESHOLD ADJUSTMENT OR RECALIBRATION WAS ATTEMPTED for the collapsed dMMR class - case-insensitive scans return zero hits for 'recalibrat' and 'calibrat', and 'threshold' returns only the AUC-versus-recall discussion and the Canny edge QC filter. So this paper documents the same discrimination-holds / decisions-collapse dissociation reported here but, unlike this project, never tests a calibration explanation; the refutation here (a 12x prior boost and unsupervised SLD-EM, both leaving Her2 at 0/14) goes further than anything in it. PREDICTION UNIT IS SLIDE and the authors flag the consequence themselves: 'slide-level splitting during cross-validation may introduce residual optimism due to shared patient-level characteristics, underscoring the importance of the independent external cohort for unbiased performance assessment.' EXTERNAL CLASS PREVALENCE IS SEVERELY SKEWED (NSMP 480 of 720 patients; POLE only 13), which the authors acknowledge for POLE - but note that the collapsed class dMMR is NOT rare externally (160 patients / 294 slides), which strengthens rather than weakens the analogy to a Her2 collapse. One point of tension with this project's own pipeline: they deliberately omit stain normalization on the grounds that it may impair foundation-model generalization, whereas stain normalisation is listed here as a candidate remediation for the Her2 collapse - so this is a cited counter-argument to that remediation, not support for it. HOW TO USE IT: context only and precedent for the failure mode, never a comparator number, because the organ is wrong. It is nonetheless the closest structural analogue anywhere: same encoder family (UNI2, Virchow2), same aggregator (CLAM MIL), a four-class molecular subtyping target, a genuine never-trained-on external cohort, the same reported metric triple (macro-AUC, macro-F1, balanced accuracy), and one class whose recall falls to 0.14 externally while its AUC holds at 0.759 (95%CI 0.718-0.800) - the same dissociation as a WSI arm's 0/14 Her2 recall at 0.86 AUROC. The authors articulate it explicitly, which gives a citable formulation: 'AUC reflects the model's ability to rank cases across decision thresholds, whereas recall reflects classification accuracy at the final subtype classification.' Two further structural corroborations: the misclassification patterns were consistent across foundation-encoder pipelines, so the failure is not encoder-specific ('suggesting that this behavior reflects an intrinsic challenge of dMMR morphology rather than a model-specific failure'); and the best encoder REORDERS between internal and external (Virchow2+CLAM best internal at 0.860, UNI2+CLAM best external at 0.780), a direct caution against selecting an encoder on internal performance.

rows.title: Scalable and Loosely-Coupled Multimodal Deep Learning for Breast Cancer Subtyping
rows.authors: Mohammed Amer, Mohamed A. Suliman, Tu Bui, Nuria Garcia, Serban Georgescu (Fujitsu Research of Europe Ltd, Slough, UK)
rows.venue: arXiv preprint, arXiv:2509.03408v1 [cs.CV], submitted 3 Sep 2025. UNREFEREED - the arXiv API record carries NO journal_ref and NO comment field, so no acceptance is claimed anywhere, on the PDF or in the metadata; the PDF uses a JMLR-style template with an empty 'Editor:' line.
rows.modalities: Four model inputs over three data types: (1) CNV, gene-level integer GISTIC-style calls from cBioPortal; (2) a WSI 'Image' representation, H&E patches through an Inceptionv3 / VGG16 / DINOv2 backbone with Inceptionv3 in the final model; (3) a WSI 'Graph' representation, HoVer-Net nuclei -> SlideGraph+ clustering -> PNA graph convolutional network; (4) EHR/clinical records via an MLP (128-64) or BERT/RoBERTa over text key-value pairs. The dual representation of the WSI as both image and graph is the paper's headline novelty, and it means the four-checkmark row is a 4-MODEL ensemble rather than a 3-modality one.
rows.datasets: TCGA-BRCA only. Verbatim: 'We evaluate our method on PAM50 breast cancer subtyping (Parker et al., 2009) using WSI, CNV, and EHR data from TCGA-BRCA. WSIs are obtained from TCGA; CNV and clinical data are obtained from cBioPortal (Cerami et al., 2012); and PAM50 labels from Netanely et al. (2016). After excluding incomplete cases, a total of 977 patients remain.' Class balance verbatim: 'The four subtypes-Luminal A (53.5%), Luminal B (20.6%), Basal-like (18.1%), and Her2-enriched (7.8%)-lead to class imbalance. To address this, we mitigate via oversampling, stratified sampling, or loss weighting.'
rows.endpoint: 4-class PAM50 molecular subtype (Luminal A / Luminal B / Basal-like / Her2-enriched). CLASS COUNT: 4, from that explicit Methods sentence naming all four with their prevalences; Normal-like is not mentioned anywhere and whether it was dropped or never present in the Netanely calls is NR. PREDICTION UNIT: case-patient - 'Each patient has multiple WSIs and patches, with patient-level labels requiring pooling of patch predictions' and 'only the top 50 tissue-rich patches per patient are used'; n is reported as 977 patients. LABEL BASIS: PAM50 labels taken from Netanely et al. (2016), i.e. RNA-derived, but the CALLING METHOD IS NR - the string 'centroid' occurs zero times in the paper and no label-derivation procedure is described. Netanely et al. is Breast Cancer Research 18:1-16, 'Expression and methylation patterns partition luminal-A breast tumors into distinct prognostic subgroups'; the task itself is cited to Parker et al. 2009.
rows.wsi_pipeline: Non-overlapping patches; tissue segmentation by HSV conversion, median blur (kernel 7) on saturation, binary threshold 20, patch accepted if more than 5% tissue. 'For efficiency, only the top 50 tissue-rich patches per patient are used.' Patch preprocessing: resize 342x342 then centre crop 299x299 for Inceptionv3 (256 to 224 for VGG16/DINOv2), rescale to [0,1], ImageNet mean/std normalisation. Weak supervision: patches inherit the patient label. Pooling evaluated at output level (majority vote, mean logits, mean probabilities) and intermediate level (mean, distance-weighted average); the reported WSI model 'uses Inceptionv3, with majority voting and weighted loss'. Graph branch: 512x512 patches -> HoVer-Net (PanNuke) 5 nuclei types -> SlideGraph+ clustering (similarity kernel, spatial threshold 2000, gamma=0.001, average linkage 0.8 cut-off), Delaunay edges at a 4000 distance threshold, PNA graph convolution, best model L=3, dims [32,16,8], lr 1e-4, p=0.2, ReLU. NO foundation-model encoder (no UNI, no CTransPath) and NO attention-MIL (no CLAM).
rows.fusion_method: Late fusion on logits. Verbatim formulation: 'o_j = sum_{i=1}^{M} w_ij * o^(i)_j + b_j' where 'w_ij are non-normalized trainable weights, and b_j is a bias term'. Two author variants: WL = Weighted Logits (no bias) and WLB = Weighted Logits with Bias. Benchmarked against WE (Weighted Ensemble; Liu et al. 2022b, Tang et al. 2024), SE (Simple Ensemble; Tang et al. 2024), MP (Max-Model Predictor; Wu et al. 2019), ML (Meta-Learning; Huang et al. 2020, Stahlschmidt et al. 2022), IF (Intermediate Fusion; Steyaert et al. 2023) and T (Transformer, 6 encoder layers, dim 512, 8 heads, one token per modality plus a CLS token). CRITICAL: 'Simple Ensemble' is NEVER DEFINED in the paper. It occurs exactly three times - once in a Related Work sentence ('Their comprehensive study explores fusion strategies like simple ensemble, weighted ensemble, and max-model predictor') and twice in the Table 2 and Table 3 captions as 'SE: Simple Ensemble (Tang et al., 2024)'. Whether SE averages logits or probabilities, and over which modalities, is NR and traceable only to FusionBench (Tang et al. 2024), which was not opened. The only safe statement is that the paper contrasts SE with the 'trainable weights' of WE/WL/WLB, so it is an untrained baseline in that sense; the paper never says so explicitly.
rows.metrics: ALL numbers are 10-fold cross-validation on TCGA-BRCA, n=977: 'Evaluation uses 10-fold cross-validation, reporting accuracy and macro-AUROC (average AUC across classes).' Whether the reported figure is pooled out-of-fold or a fold-mean is NR, and no standard deviations or confidence intervals are given anywhere. TABLE 1 (single modality; Accuracy | Macro-AUC): CNV 70.25 | 0.8284; WSI Image 66.96 | 0.8080; WSI Graph 70.23 | 0.8350; Clinical 70.43 | 0.8522. CLINICAL IS THE STRONGEST SINGLE MODALITY on both metrics, confirmed both by the ordering and in text: 'The highest accuracy achieved by a single-modality model is 70.43%, whereas our multimodal approach, utilizing all available modalities, achieves 78.13%. Similarly, for macro-AUC, the best single-modality performance reaches 0.8522, while multimodal fusion boosts it to 0.9153.' TABLE 3 (Macro-AUC; columns WE SE MP ML IF T WL* WLB*), row identity verified from checkmark positions in a layout-preserving extraction: [Image+Graph] 0.8465 0.8569 0.8506 0.8274 0.8128 0.8220 0.8616(dagger) 0.8604; [CNV+Image] 0.8728 0.8738 0.8610 0.8692 0.8432 0.8589 0.8835 0.8836(dagger); [CNV+Image+Graph] 0.8736 0.8931 0.8730 0.8794 0.8349 0.8395 0.9000(dagger) 0.8995; [CNV+Image+Clinical] 0.8965 0.9074(dagger) 0.8873 0.8912 0.8429 0.8592 0.8976 0.9008; [CNV+Image+Graph+Clinical] 0.8978 0.9153 0.8889 0.9006 0.8369 0.8541 0.9153 0.9153(dagger). Caption: 'Best performance is bolded and marked with dagger.' So in the CNV+image+clinical row the untrained Simple Ensemble 0.9074 carries the dagger and beats the authors' own WL* 0.8976 and WLB* 0.9008; and in the all-modality row SE 0.9153 TIES WL* 0.9153 and WLB* 0.9153 exactly, with the dagger on WLB*. The authors concede it: 'Regarding macro-AUC, our method surpasses SOTA in nearly all cases, except for one combination-CNV, image, and clinical data-where it is the second best performance.' TABLE 2 (Accuracy; same columns and row order): [Image+Graph] 68.57 68.64 68.44 66.52 66.23 66.02 68.68 69.51(dagger); [CNV+Image] 72.57 73.24 73.14 71.96 70.97 73.54 75.41(dagger) 75.12; [CNV+Image+Graph] 73.3 74.52 73.72 74.12 71.66 71.87 76.41(dagger) 76.23; [CNV+Image+Clinical] 74.10 76.23 74.73 75.10 72.08 73.49 76.88(dagger) 76.78; [CNV+Image+Graph+Clinical] 73.96 76.91 74.76 77.15 71.37 74.25 77.92 78.13(dagger). On ACCURACY the authors' WL/WLB carries the dagger in every row including CNV+image+clinical; SE beats them only on macro-AUC. Interpretability of the learned late-fusion weights: 'contributions from WSI-based CNN and graph models collectively account for more than half of the prediction scores, with the graph model having the highest attribution (28%) and the CNN model the lowest (23.75%).' CNV branch: gene-level discrete integers in {-2,-1,0,1,2} with genes carrying missing values removed, fed to 'an SNN with 8192-2048 channel layers and oversampling'; the gene count after filtering is NR.
rows.external_validation: NONE. A case-insensitive count over the complete extracted full text returns ZERO occurrences of 'CPTAC', zero of 'METABRIC', zero of 'external valid', zero of 'held-out'/'held out' and zero of 'independent test'. Every result in the paper is 10-fold CV on TCGA-BRCA; there is no held-out cohort, no second institution and no external test set of any kind.
rows.code: NR - no code-availability statement, no repository URL, and no data-availability section beyond the TCGA acknowledgement.
rows.caveats: UNREFEREED PREPRINT - arXiv:2509.03408v1, cs.CV, 3 Sep 2025, with no journal_ref and no comment field in the arXiv record, so no venue acceptance is claimed. (1) 'Simple Ensemble' is used as a baseline but never defined; its exact operator (logit mean vs probability mean) is NR and traceable only to FusionBench. (2) No confidence intervals, no standard deviations across the 10 folds and no significance test anywhere - so 'SE 0.9074 beats WL 0.8976' is an unquantified difference, not a demonstrated one. (3) Whether the reported figure is pooled out-of-fold or a fold-mean is NR. (4) The CNV branch is GENE-LEVEL discrete calls, not arm-level, and the gene count after 'removing genes with missing values' is NR. (5) The strongest single modality is CLINICAL (0.8522), not CNV, which reframes the paper's own 'multimodal fusion helps' claim, since the headline 0.9153 is a +0.063 gain over clinical alone. (6) The WSI branch is Inceptionv3 patch classification with majority voting over 50 patches, roughly a 2019-era pipeline rather than attention-MIL over foundation-model features, so its 0.8080 is a weak WSI arm and not a like-for-like stand-in for a CLAM + UNI2-h arm. (7) The ladder treats image and graph as two SEPARATE WSI models. HOW TO USE IT: fair comparator to the INTERNAL TCGA numbers only, with the caveat that Amer's macro-AUC is 10-fold CV on 977 patients over a differently-derived label set and a much weaker WSI encoder; IRRELEVANT as a comparator to any external number, since the paper has no external cohort at all. The single most useful fact: Amer's OWN Table 3 shows the untrained Simple Ensemble (0.9074) beating both of their trained fusion operators (0.8976, 0.9008) in the CNV+image+clinical row and tying them at 0.9153 in the all-modality row, with the authors conceding it in text. That is an independent, in-domain instance of the untrained average beating the trained operator, reported by a group that did not set out to show it, and it is the only such instance in the WSI+CNV PAM50 literature. Their CNV-alone 0.8284 is a near comparator to a CNV-alone 0.866 internal / 0.888 external, with the caveat that theirs is gene-level GISTIC calls through an 8192-2048 SNN and this project's is 39 arm medians through logistic regression - roughly a 500-fold difference in feature dimensionality and the opposite end of the assay-cost spectrum.

rows.title: M3FusionNet: Cross-cohort multimodal prediction of breast cancer biomarkers
rows.authors: Vinita Shah, Miral Patel (The Charutar Vidya Mandal (CVM) University, Anand, Gujarat, India)
rows.venue: Computational Biology and Chemistry (Elsevier), vol. 124, issue 'Pt 2', article 109228. Refereed. Crossref gives published-print [[2026, 10]] - year and month only, with no day; Europe PMC gives firstPublicationDate 2026-07-05, PMID 42407417 and no PMCID.
rows.modalities: From the abstract only: 'integrating haematoxylin-and-eosin (H&E) whole slide images (WSIs), RNA-seq, miRNA, proteomics, and clinical variables'. COPY NUMBER IS NOT NAMED among the modalities in the abstract, and no CNV or copy-number term appears in the Europe PMC keyword list either ('Breast cancer, Proteomics, Whole Slide Imaging, Tcga, Cptac, Biomarker Prediction, Computational Pathology, Proteogenomic Integration, Multimodal Deep Learning, Xgboost, Domain Generalisation, M3fusionnet'); whether a CNV branch exists in the body is UNVERIFIED. Proteomics is described as 'CPTAC-exclusive', i.e. present in only one of the two cohorts.
rows.datasets: From the abstract only: 'TCGA-BRCA n ~ 1036) and CPTAC-BRCA (n ~ 134)' - the unbalanced parenthesis is in the published text, and both figures are given by the authors themselves as approximations. Whether n counts patients, cases or slides is NR.
rows.endpoint: Five biomarkers predicted simultaneously: ER, PR, HER2, PAM50 molecular subtype (classification) and MKI67/Ki-67 (continuous regression). PAM50 is one of five heads and not the paper's primary endpoint. CLASS COUNT: NR - the abstract says only 'molecular subtypes (PAM50)' and later mentions 'HER2-enriched and triple-negative subtypes', mixing PAM50 and IHC vocabulary in one sentence; whether the head is 4-class or 5-class cannot be established from the abstract and there is no released code or output layer to inspect. PREDICTION UNIT: NR - the abstract gives n ~ 1036 and n ~ 134 without stating whether these are patients, cases or slides, and never says whether the AUCs are slide-level or case-level. That is a material gap, since the CPTAC arm here is 378 slides mapping to 114 cases and slide-level scoring on the same data would not be comparable. LABEL BASIS: NR - the abstract names PAM50 as a target but does not state the caller for either cohort. Since RNA-seq is among the input modalities and PAM50 is RNA-derived by construction, the label provenance is exactly the fact needed to judge leakage, and it is unobtainable.
rows.wsi_pipeline: From the abstract only: 'Feature extraction from WSIs was performed using ResNet50 (2,048-dimensional embeddings), with subsequent feature-level fusion across modalities.' Domain adaptation is named as 'Macenko stain normalisation and ComBat batch correction'. Tiling geometry, magnification, patch size, bag construction, MIL aggregator and slide-to-case pooling are ALL NR.
rows.fusion_method: From the abstract only: 'feature-level fusion across modalities', downstream of which 'Gradient-boosted models (XGBoost, CatBoost) were employed for both classification (ER, PR, HER2, PAM50) and continuous regression (MKI67).' No fusion operator is named beyond 'feature-level', and no untrained-average baseline is mentioned.
rows.metrics: ABSTRACT ONLY - the body and all tables are behind the Elsevier paywall (see caveats), so every number below is UNVERIFIED against the body and carries the abstract's own thin split description. Retrieved from the Europe PMC REST core record (resultType=core, HTTP 200, hitCount 1, pmid 42407417). VERBATIM: 'In-distribution performance on TCGA reached AUC values of 0.99 (ER), 0.96 (PR), 0.98 (HER2), and 0.96 (PAM50 macro-AUC), with an overall AUC of 0.97.' SPLIT TYPE NR - the word used is 'in-distribution', and whether this is cross-validation, a held-out TCGA test split, or training-set performance is NOT stated. VERBATIM: 'Cross-dataset generalisation exhibited a controlled 13-22% AUC reduction (E1: Overall AUC 0.82), substantially mitigated by harmonised preprocessing and multimodal fusion' - the 0.82 is an OVERALL AUC POOLED ACROSS THE FIVE ENDPOINTS, not a PAM50-specific number, and no PAM50 macro-AUC under E1 appears in the abstract. VERBATIM: 'The combined TCGA + CPTAC model (M3FusionNet-E3) demonstrated superior robustness with Overall AUC of 0.90, particularly for HER2-enriched and triple-negative subtypes.' VERBATIM: 'Proteomics integration (CPTAC-exclusive) improved HER2 AUC by 2-3 %age points' (the '%age' typo is in the source); whether this refers to the HER2 biomarker head or the PAM50 HER2-enriched class, and under which protocol, is not stated. NO per-class AUC, NO confidence interval, NO balanced accuracy, NO sample-level recall and NO PAM50-specific external number is present in the abstract.
rows.external_validation: THE DECIDING QUESTION IS UNRESOLVED. The abstract states 'M3FusionNet is evaluated through three experimental protocols spanning TCGA-BRCA n ~ 1036) and CPTAC-BRCA (n ~ 134)' but names only two of the three - E1 and E3. E1 is labelled 'Cross-dataset generalisation ... (E1: Overall AUC 0.82)', consistent with train-TCGA/test-CPTAC but NOT stated in those words. E3 IS explicitly a POOLED model - 'The combined TCGA + CPTAC model (M3FusionNet-E3) demonstrated superior robustness with Overall AUC of 0.90' - so E3's 0.90 is NOT an external number: CPTAC is inside its training data by the authors' own description. Whether ANY PAM50-specific number exists under E1 in the body's tables is UNVERIFIED and cannot be resolved without the paywalled text. On the evidence obtainable, the claim that no published multimodal PAM50 model has an external, never-trained-on, PAM50-specific evaluation is NOT broken by this paper - but it is also NOT verified against it, and that gap should be stated in the thesis rather than papered over.
rows.code: NR - no code or data availability statement is present in the Europe PMC record, and Unpaywall reports oa_status 'closed' with has_repository_copy false, so no preprint or repository copy exists to check.
rows.caveats: PAYWALL, FULLY BLOCKING, three independent observations recorded: (1) the Europe PMC REST core record returns a fullTextUrlList with a single entry, availability 'Subscription required', availabilityCode 'S', pmcid null, inEPMC N, isOpenAccess N; (2) paper-search read europepmc PMID:42407417 fails with 'does not have an accessible PDF'; (3) WebFetch of https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1476927126003555 returns HTTP 403 Forbidden - the DOI resolves via linkinghub.elsevier.com to that PII with HTTP 200 on the redirect stub only. Unpaywall for the DOI returns is_oa false, oa_status 'closed', oa_locations [] and has_repository_copy false; Semantic Scholar reports openAccessPdf status CLOSED; and a paper-search sweep across crossref, openalex, semantic, europepmc and base plus two web-search passes found NO preprint, repository or alternative version. The body is genuinely unreachable. EVERYTHING BELOW THE ABSTRACT REMAINS UNVERIFIED: the existence or value of a PAM50-specific E1 (TCGA to CPTAC) macro-AUC; the definition of protocol E2; the exact E3 pooling sentence; whether CNV is a modality; the PAM50 class count and label caller; case- versus slide-level evaluation; and the per-class HER2 numbers. None of these was filled from a search-engine snippet. FURTHER CONCERNS visible from the abstract alone: two authors from a single institution; TCGA in-distribution AUCs of 0.99/0.98/0.96 with RNA-seq in the feature set invite the same target-leakage question this project documents for RNA-to-PAM50, and the abstract gives no indication the authors considered it; and 'Overall AUC' pooled across five heterogeneous endpoints (four classification, one regression) is not a standard or interpretable metric. Refereed. HOW TO USE IT: near comparator needing a caveat - potentially to the headline external numbers here - but UNUSABLE as a tabulated comparator on present evidence.
