Reasons: the only PAM50-specific number obtainable is the internal TCGA 0.96 macro-AUC with split type NR, which is not comparable to anything; the only cross-cohort number obtainable, E1 Overall AUC 0.82, is pooled over five endpoints and is therefore NOT a PAM50 macro-AUROC and must never be placed beside 0.909; and E3's 0.90 is explicitly a combined TCGA+CPTAC model, i.e. CPTAC in training, which is exactly the pooling this design forbids and which the reporting rules here require to be labelled. RECOMMENDED HANDLING: cite it as the nearest existing cross-cohort multimodal breast work, state that its E3 protocol pools CPTAC into training, and state honestly that whether an E1 PAM50-specific number exists could not be verified because the full text is behind an Elsevier paywall (HTTP 403) with no open copy - rather than asserting the negative. Do NOT weaken the novelty claim on the strength of an abstract, and do not strengthen it either.

rows.title: Genetic determinants of the molecular portraits of epithelial cancers
rows.authors: Youli Xia, Cheng Fan, Katherine A. Hoadley, Joel S. Parker, Charles M. Perou (University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center)
rows.venue: Nature Communications, volume 10, article number 5666, published 11 December 2019. Refereed, open access CC BY. Crossref confirms container-title, volume 10, issue 1, article-number 5666, issued 2019-12-11 and the CC BY licence; Europe PMC carries PMC6906458 / PMID 31827079.
rows.modalities: Single modality: somatic DNA copy number alterations only. NO imaging of any kind. The predicted TARGETS span RNA expression signatures, RPPA protein levels, IHC receptor status, somatic mutations and intrinsic molecular subtype.
rows.datasets: TCGA-BRCA n=1038 (matched expression and copy number, Normal-like EXCLUDED) split into a balanced 70% training set and 30% test set; METABRIC n=1689 (Normal-like excluded; the full METABRIC expression set is n=1992) as the independent validation cohort. Also TCGA lung (LUAD n=498 + LUSC n=512) and a 25-tumour-type / 10,635-sample pan-cancer extension.
rows.endpoint: Multiple. The relevant one is breast intrinsic (PAM50) molecular subtype, modelled as FOUR SEPARATE BINARY one-vs-rest classifiers (Basal-like, HER2-Enriched, Luminal A, Luminal B). Also 543 gene expression signatures, three commercial assay scores (OncotypeDX, Prosigna ROR, MammaPrint), 216 RPPA proteins, ER/PR/HER2 IHC status, IDC-vs-ILC histology, somatic mutations and tumour mutation burden. CLASS COUNT: 4 for the breast intrinsic-subtype analysis, with Normal-like excluded by construction ('two independent statistical tests were used on TCGA breast cancer cohort with matched gene expression and copy number data excluding all Normal-like samples (n = 1038)'; 'For breast cancer gene expression signatures, Normal-like samples were excluded (n = 1038)') - but crucially the four are NOT a 4-way head: each is a separate binary outcome, 'For molecular subtype, clinical receptor status, cancer histology, and mutations that had binary outcomes, models were built to classify each outcome.' PREDICTION UNIT: case-patient (bulk tumour sample); no imaging, no patches, no slides; TCGA n=1038 samples and METABRIC n=1689 samples. LABEL BASIS: RNA-derived PAM50 by nearest-centroid, with cohort-specific calling described verbatim - 'To determine breast cancer intrinsic PAM50 subtypes for TCGA breast cancer data, the TCGA RNA-seq data were first subsampled to match the ER distribution of the training set used for PAM50. Then the entire data set were adjusted to the median gene expression calculated for the PAM50 genes determined from the ER balanced subset. Intrinsic subtyping was then done as previously described' and, for the validation cohort, 'For METABRIC, median-centered and standardized gene expression were used to calculate correlation to each subtype centroid'. So both cohorts carry expression-derived PAM50 calls and the two callers differ in their normalisation step - the same class of cross-cohort label heterogeneity a TCGA/CPTAC pair has.
rows.wsi_pipeline: N/A - no imaging.
rows.fusion_method: N/A - single modality, no fusion.
rows.metrics: FEATURES: 'Instead of using gene-level CNA scores as predictors, we calculated 536 segment-level CNA scores using predefined chromosome regions that have been shown to be important in cancers (Supplementary Data 2). These DNA segments included pan-cancer significant somatic CNAs as well as breast cancer subtype-specific CNA regions', with 'Each segment score was calculated as the mean CNA score across genes within the segment.' SPLIT PROTOCOL: 'The 1038 sample TCGA breast cancer data set was split into a balanced training set (70%) and test set (30%). Models were built solely on TCGA training set and validated on both TCGA test set as well as on a large independent breast tumor data set from the Molecular Taxonomy of Breast Cancer International Consortium (METABRIC, n = 1689).' The 70/30 split is a SINGLE stratified random draw (R package sampling, stratified on overall survival, gender, race, ER/PR/HER2 status, histological subtype, pathologic stage and molecular subtype where available); hyperparameters were tuned by '200 rounds of Monte-Carlo cross validation with default training percentage of 0.75 (R package caret)' INSIDE the training set only. INTRINSIC SUBTYPE AUCs, verbatim and INCOMPLETE IN THE SOURCE: 'Prediction models for all intrinsic subtypes demonstrated high AUC values (i.e., >0.75)'; 'The Basal-like subtype had the highest test set AUC values (>0.9)'; 'HER2-Enriched subtype also had high AUC values (>0.82)'; 'Luminal A and Luminal B subtypes were harder to predict, yet were still highly predictable (AUC for Luminal A = 0.82, and for Luminal B = 0.76 on the METABRIC validation set).' Basal-like and HER2-Enriched are therefore given only as INEQUALITIES and without an unambiguous cohort label; their exact point values live in Supplementary Fig. 6a-d and Supplementary Data 4, which are not in the Europe PMC XML and were NOT opened, so those two point estimates are UNVERIFIED. LumA 0.82 and LumB 0.76 are the only exact subtype figures in the body and both are METABRIC. No confidence intervals are reported for any subtype AUC. COMMERCIAL ASSAY REPLACEMENT: 'Three research-based implementations of commercially available signatures that are commonly used in the breast cancer clinic, namely OncotypeDX recurrence score, Prosigna risk of recurrence score and MAMMAPRINT 70-GENE recurrence score, were all highly predictable using CNAs with corresponding METABRIC test set AUC values of 0.79, 0.81, and 0.87', with the targets dichotomised as 'samples with high scores (top third) versus low scores (bottom two-thirds)' on the RESEARCH-BASED expression score rather than a commercial assay result. RECEPTOR STATUS: 'our Elastic Net models were able to accurately predict ER RPPA protein expression (AUC 0.82) and ER clinical IHC status (AUC 0.89 on METABRIC validation set) when making use of DNA copy number information only.' OTHER CONTEXT NUMBERS, all verified: 142 of 543 signatures had AUC > 0.75 in both test sets; the permutation null reached a maximum AUC of 0.63; the 16q23-amplicon signature reached 0.96 (METABRIC validation); HER1-C2 reached 0.90 in both test sets; a CD8 T-cell signature and a stroma signature 'selected no CNA features and had AUC value of 0.5'; the CD8 T-cell signature reached 0.74 on all samples against 0.88 on Basal-only; IDC-vs-ILC histology 0.87 training / 0.8 test; LUAD-vs-LUSC 0.98 training / 0.97 test; multi-tumour Claudin-low 0.8 training / 0.74 test; and restricting features to the 313-gene Foundation One panel 'achieved essentially identical results and AUC values'.
rows.external_validation: YES, and genuinely held out across BOTH assay platforms: 'Models were built solely on TCGA training set and validated on both TCGA test set as well as on a large independent breast tumor data set from ... (METABRIC, n = 1689).' The platform change is real and is the paper's own selling point: TCGA copy number is 'GISTIC2 gene-level copy number data ... acquired from The Broad Institute TCGA GDAC Firehose with no further processing (all_data_by_genes.txt)', while METABRIC is 'copy number segmentation data using circular binary segmentation (CBS) algorithm ... Using Ensembl 54 (hg18) genome build, gene-level copy number score were derived through the extreme method as used in GISTIC2'; expression platforms differ too (TCGA mRNA-seq vs METABRIC Illumina HT-29 v3 microarray). The Discussion says so: 'we were able to predict many of these signatures with very high accuracy (AUC > 0.9) on a true test set that even used different gene expression and DNA copy number technologies (i.e., METABRIC).' Nothing indicates METABRIC entered training.
rows.code: https://github.com/xyouli/DNA-based-predictors-of-non-genetic-cancer-phenotypes - 'All code supporting the current study is deposited in GitHub. All computational analyses are done using public R packages.' Data: TCGA via Broad GDAC Firehose; METABRIC via EGA at EBI.
rows.caveats: ACCESS NOTE: nature.com returned HTTP 303 See Other redirecting to idp.nature.com/authorize (cross-host, not followed); the full text was obtained from the Europe PMC REST endpoint /PMC6906458/fullTextXML at HTTP 200, and note that both paper-search read pmc PMC6906458 and read europepmc PMC6906458 FAIL with 'does not have an open access PDF', so the CLI alone would have wrongly recorded this paper as unreachable. UNVERIFIED: the exact point AUCs for Basal-like and HER2-Enriched, and the per-subtype TCGA-test-set values, live in Supplementary Fig. 6 and Supplementary Data 4, which are not in the XML and were not opened. THE METRIC CAVEAT IS THE WHOLE STORY: these are one-vs-rest BINARY AUCs from four independent Elastic Net models, one per subtype. There is no multiclass model, no argmax decision, no confusion matrix, no balanced accuracy and no macro AUROC anywhere - the string 'macro' occurs zero times in the full text. Also: the split is a single stratified 70/30 draw, so there are no fold-to-fold or seed-to-seed error bars on any number. COMPETING INTERESTS declared and relevant: 'C.M.P is an equity stock holder and consultant of BioClassifier LLC. C.M.P and J.S.P are listed as an inventor on patent applications on the Breast PAM50 assay' - relevant because the paper reports how well a DNA assay can replace the authors' own RNA assay. Refereed. HOW TO USE IT: near comparator needing a caveat, against the CNV-only arm. THE CAVEAT IS NON-NEGOTIABLE AND MUST TRAVEL WITH EVERY QUOTATION: Xia et al. report ONE-VS-REST BINARY AUC from four independent binary models, never a 4-class macro AUROC. A per-subtype OvR AUC and a macro AUROC are not the same quantity and the two must never appear in the same column. What the paper legitimately establishes: (i) copy number alone predicts breast intrinsic subtype well enough to matter, and (ii) it does so ACROSS platforms - TCGA GISTIC2 gene-level to METABRIC CBS segments, mRNA-seq to microarray - which is structurally the TCGA(SNP6/GISTIC)-to-CPTAC(WGS) design here and directly supports the per-arm r = 0.960 platform-difference finding; (iii) their per-subtype ordering (Basal >0.9 > HER2-E >0.82 > LumA 0.82 > LumB 0.76) matches qualitatively, including LumB as the hardest class; (iv) the assay-replacement numbers (Prosigna ROR 0.81, OncotypeDX 0.79, MammaPrint 0.87 on METABRIC) are the ONLY quantitative precedent found anywhere for the 'cheap DNA assay substitutes for an expensive RNA assay' framing, and belong in the motivation rather than the results. FEATURE-GRANULARITY DISTINCTION WORTH MAKING: they use 536 predefined segment-level scores drawn from published pan-cancer and breast-subtype-specific regions, and their figure captions repeatedly say 'Elastic net selected CNA segments and/or whole chromosomal arms and their coefficients' - so whole arms are ELIGIBLE features inside a 536-feature space, but NO ARM-ONLY FEATURE SET IS EVER EVALUATED ALONE anywhere in the paper. A 39-arm-only model is therefore not pre-empted: it is a strictly coarser, deliberately sWGS-reachable restriction they never tested.

rows.title: Identification of the copy number variant biomarkers for breast cancer subtypes
rows.authors: Xiaoyong Pan, XiaoHua Hu, Yu-Hang Zhang, Lei Chen, LiuCun Zhu, ShiBao Wan, Tao Huang, Yu-Dong Cai (Shanghai University; Erasmus MC Rotterdam; Fudan University; Chinese Academy of Sciences)
rows.venue: Molecular Genetics and Genomics (Springer), volume 294, issue 1, pages 95-110. Refereed. Crossref gives published and published-online date-parts [[2018,9,10]] and published-print [[2019,2]], so the online-first year is 2018 and the issue year 2019; PubMed (PMID 30203254) and Europe PMC index the issue year as 2019.
rows.modalities: Single modality: copy number variation only. No imaging, no expression, no clinical variables in the model.
rows.datasets: METABRIC n=1608 as TRAINING set; TCGA n=499 as INDEPENDENT TEST set. Verbatim: 'We downloaded the CNV data from two large breast cancer databases, METABRIC and TCGA. To construct a more stringent dataset, we used 1608 samples from METABRIC as training set and 499 samples from TCGA as test set (Table 1). Each sample was encoded using the copy numbers of 20,649 probes.' Table 1, 'Details of training and test set used in this study', per-class counts: Training / METABRIC - Basal 209, Her2 224, LumA 700, LumB 475, Total 1608; Test / TCGA - Basal 92, Her2 56, LumA 224, LumB 127, Total 499. Both rows sum correctly and the grand total 2107 is consistent with the abstract's 'more than 2000 samples'. Data provenance is cited only as '(Ciriello et al. 2015; Milioli et al. 2016a, b)'.
rows.endpoint: 4-class breast cancer subtype: Basal, Her2, LumA, LumB - exactly this project's four class names. CLASS COUNT: 4, from the Methods opening ('We first collected CNV data for breast cancer subtypes basal, Her2, LumA, and LumB from two large databases'), from Table 1's four label columns, and from the per-class accuracy sentences. NOTE an internal self-contradiction: the Introduction separately describes a FIVE-category IHC scheme (luminal A, luminal B, luminal/Her2, Her2-enriched, basal-like) which is NOT the scheme used. PREDICTION UNIT: sample, i.e. a bulk tumour - the paper says 'samples' throughout and never says 'patients'; no imaging, so no slide or patch question arises. LABEL BASIS: NR, and this is the deciding fact that could not be established from the full text. What the paper actually says: the Methods state only 'We first collected CNV data for breast cancer subtypes basal, Her2, LumA, and LumB from two large databases' and 'We downloaded the CNV data from two large breast cancer databases, METABRIC and TCGA', with no sentence anywhere defining how a sample was assigned to a subtype. The only subtype DEFINITION in the paper is the Introduction's IHC/Ki-67 surrogate, verbatim: 'luminal A (ER positive and/or PR positive and Ki-67 < 14%), luminal B (ER positive and/or PR positive and Ki-67 >= 14%), luminal/Her2 (ER positive and/or PR positive and Her2 positive), Her2-enriched (ER negative and PR negative and Her2 positive), and basal-like (ER negative and PR negative and Her2 negative)' - which names FIVE categories, not the four modelled, so it cannot be the operative label definition. Circumstantially the data citations point the other way, since Milioli et al. 2016b is an expression-based intrinsic-subtype paper on METABRIC and Ciriello et al. 2015 is the TCGA lobular breast cancer paper that carries PAM50 calls; and the paper treats PAM50 as an EXTERNAL reference set it compares its selected genes against ('We compared the PAM50 gene list with our optimal copy number variation-associated genes'), which reads as though PAM50 is not its own label source. Scans for 'nearest centroid' and 'annotat' return zero hits. Expression-derived intrinsic subtype is the more likely reading but is NOT STATED; recorded as NR.
rows.wsi_pipeline: N/A - no imaging.
rows.fusion_method: N/A - single modality, no fusion. The pipeline is Monte Carlo Feature Selection for ranking, then two-stage Incremental Feature Selection over feature-count intervals, with a dagging classifier (Ting and Witten 1997) as the learner and a Nearest Neighbour Algorithm classifier as the comparison method; rough-set / Johnson Reducer rule learning emits human-readable IF-THEN rules.
rows.metrics: NO AUROC AND NO ROC ANALYSIS ANYWHERE, established by case-SENSITIVE counts over the complete 78,920-character rendered article text: 'AUC' 0, 'ROC' 0, 'AUROC' 0, 'area under' 0, 'receiver operating' 0. (A case-insensitive search is misleading here because it matches 'proc' inside 'process' and 'procedure'.) The metrics are Matthews correlation coefficient, defined in the paper as a MULTICLASS MCC by the covariance form MCC = cov(X,Y)/sqrt(cov(X,X)cov(Y,Y)), plus weighted-average F1 and accuracy. DAGGING, the selected model, tenfold cross-validation on the METABRIC TRAINING set: 'When the first 8715 features were selected, the highest MCC value was 0.515 and the corresponding weighted-average F1 score was 0.664' (an earlier coarser sweep gave 'The highest MCC by testing the above-mentioned feature sets was 0.513, which was produced by the feature set containing top 8810 features'). Per-class accuracy under the same tenfold CV: 'The accuracy for four subtypes (Basal, Her2, LumA, and LumB) yielded by the optimal classifier was 0.684, 0.429, 0.864, and 0.507, respectively, and the overall accuracy and weighted-average F1 score were 0.675 and 0.664, respectively.' INDEPENDENT TEST on TCGA: 'we evaluated its performance on the independent test set derived from TCGA, which yielded an MCC value of 0.492, an overall accuracy of 0.647, and a weighted-average F1 score of 0.653. These values were all quite close to those on the training set, suggesting that the generalizability of the optimal classifier was quite good.' NO per-class breakdown is given for the TCGA independent test set - only those three aggregate numbers. NNA comparison classifier: tenfold-CV MCC 0.352 with the top 20 features, weighted-average F1 0.518, per-class accuracies 'basal, Her2, LumA, and LumB ... 0.502, 0.594, 0.834, and 0.164', overall accuracy 0.560; independent test 'MCC 0.349, overall accuracy 0.557 and weighted-average F1 score 0.545'. No confidence intervals, no standard deviations across folds and no significance test anywhere.
rows.external_validation: YES, and it is a true held-out independent cohort with no pooling. Design verbatim: 'To construct a more stringent dataset, we used 1608 samples from METABRIC as training set and 499 samples from TCGA as test set (Table 1).' Both feature-selection stages and all tenfold cross-validation run inside METABRIC only; TCGA appears solely in the sentence 'we evaluated its performance on the independent test set derived from TCGA'. Nothing in the text suggests TCGA data enters MCFS ranking, IFS selection or classifier fitting. This is a cleaner cross-cohort separation than most of the survey.
rows.code: NR - no code repository. Supporting material is Supplementary Materials S1-S3 (feature rankings and the MCC/F1 curves), referenced but not fetched.
rows.caveats: PROVENANCE, AND IT MATTERS BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS ACCESS ROUTE DOES NOT WORK: the full text was read from the mirror https://rd.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00438-018-1488-4 (HTTP 200, 658,293 bytes, complete Introduction through References), and Table 1 from https://rd.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00438-018-1488-4/tables/1 (HTTP 200, 241,258 bytes). link.springer.com serves only a 3,038-byte JavaScript bot-challenge page to non-browser clients (HTTP 200) and a 303 redirect to idp.springer.com to WebFetch, and the /tables/1 path there returns the same challenge. The article is CLOSED access - Unpaywall is_oa false, oa_status closed, oa_locations [], has_repository_copy false; Semantic Scholar openAccessPdf status CLOSED; Europe PMC has no PMCID - so there is no institutional entitlement behind this reading, only the mirror. THE DECIDING FACT IS UNRESOLVED - see the label-basis discussion in the endpoint field; if the labels are IHC-defined this is a different endpoint from RNA-derived PAM50 and belongs in a different row of any table. OTHER CONCERNS: (1) retaining 8715 of 20,649 features is not feature selection in any meaningful sense - the 'optimal' model uses 42% of the probe set, and the MCC curve is described as flat ('they first follow a sharp increasing trend and become stable'), so 8715 is a peak on a plateau rather than an identified biomarker set; (2) Her2 per-class accuracy is 0.429 under tenfold CV and LumB 0.507, so the aggregate 0.675 is carried almost entirely by LumA (0.864, the majority class at 43.5% of the training set); (3) the paper reports NO per-class numbers on the TCGA independent test set, which is exactly where the interesting failure would show; (4) the 'quantitative distinctive rules' section is largely post-hoc literature justification of individual genes. Refereed. HOW TO USE IT: near comparator needing a caveat - structurally the closest published design to a CNV-only arm (single-modality CNV, 4-class, exactly these class names, one cohort for training and a genuinely independent second cohort for test), but NOT tabulatable against any number here, for two hard reasons. (i) IT REPORTS NO AUROC AT ALL. Its currency is multiclass MCC (0.515 tenfold CV on METABRIC, 0.492 on the TCGA independent test), weighted-average F1 (0.664 / 0.653) and accuracy (0.675 / 0.647); none converts to a macro AUROC, and its overall accuracy 0.647 is not a balanced accuracy either, since accuracy on a set that is 45% LumA is not balanced accuracy. The only defensible cross-reference is qualitative: its cross-cohort MCC drop is small (0.515 to 0.492), the same 'CNV transports across cohorts' shape as 0.866 to 0.888 here, and its per-class ordering (LumA 0.864 >> Basal 0.684 > LumB 0.507 > Her2 0.429 under CV) is the mirror image of a CNV arm that recovers 12/14 Her2 externally. (ii) THE LABEL BASIS IS UNSTATED, so whether it is even the same task is unresolved. USE: cite it as the counterweight to inflated CNV-only claims - a modest external MCC of 0.492 from 8715 gene-level features is a useful foil to any near-perfect single-modality result - and to make the point that a 42%-of-the-probe-set feature space does not buy what 39 arm medians buy. Do NOT place its numbers in the same table as any AUROC.

rows.title: CNApp, a tool for the quantification of copy number alterations and integrative analysis revealing clinical implications
rows.authors: Sebastia Franch-Exposito, Laia Bassaganyas, Maria Vila-Casadesus, Eva Hernandez-Illan, Roger Esteban-Fabro, Marcos Diaz-Gay, Juan Jose Lozano, Antoni Castells, Josep Maria Llovet, Sergi Castellvi-Bel, Jordi Camps (IDIBAPS / Hospital Clinic de Barcelona; Mount Sinai; ICREA)
rows.venue: eLife 2020;9:e50267, published 15 January 2020 (received 17 July 2019, accepted 14 January 2020). Refereed, with a named Reviewing Editor and Senior Editor and a published decision letter. Open access CC BY. Europe PMC PMC7010409 / PMID 31939734.
rows.modalities: Single modality: segmented somatic copy number data (log2 ratio seg.mean per segment, optionally with tumour purity and B-allele frequency). No imaging, and no expression as a model input - expression enters only as the source of the CMS labels being predicted.
rows.datasets: TCGA pan-cancer n=10,635 samples spanning 33 cancer types (Affymetrix SNP6.0 Level 3 segments from GDC); TCGA-LIHC n=370 for the recurrent-CNA benchmark against GISTIC2.0; TCGA-COAD n=309 with known CMS (CMS1 64, CMS2 112, CMS3 51, CMS4 82) and n=297 with MSI status (MSI 72, MSS 225); and an independent CRC validation cohort (Berg et al. 2019) n=147 (MSI 28, MSS 119; CMS1 27, CMS2 61, CMS3 29, CMS4 30). BREAST CANCER APPEARS ONLY as one of the 33 pan-cancer types, in a single descriptive sentence; there is no breast subtype analysis of any kind.
rows.endpoint: Two prediction endpoints, both COLORECTAL: colorectal consensus molecular subtype CMS1-CMS4 (Guinney et al. 2015), and microsatellite instability status (MSI vs MSS). Plus descriptive pan-cancer characterisation of CNA burden by tumour type. CLASS COUNT: 4 for CMS - 'A representative cohort of 309 colon cancers from the TCGA Colon Adenocarcinoma (COAD) cohort with known CMS classification (CMS1, N = 64; CMS2 N = 112; CMS3 N = 51; CMS4 N = 82)' - and 2 for MSI. NOT a PAM50 class count; the paper has no breast subtype analysis. PREDICTION UNIT: case-patient, one segmented copy number profile per tumour sample; no imaging, no slides. LABEL BASIS: other, and not breast - CMS labels are expression-signature-derived colorectal consensus molecular subtypes from Guinney et al. 2015, supplied to the authors externally and acknowledged as such ('The authors thank Dr. Rodrigo Dienstmann ... for providing CMS and clinical information for the subset of samples included in the COAD cohort from TCGA'); MSI labels are the TCGA-annotated microsatellite status.
rows.wsi_pipeline: N/A - no imaging.
rows.fusion_method: N/A - single modality, no fusion. The classifier is randomForest (R randomForest package); the Classifier model's documented default protocol is 'model construction is performed 50-times, in which training sets of 75% of samples are used in each permutation and the remaining 25% are classified by applying the trained model'.
rows.metrics: BURDEN SCORE DEFINITIONS, the reason this row exists, all verbatim from Methods 'CNA scores computation'. Segment classification: 'Using default parameters, segments are tagged as chromosomal when 90% or more of the chromosome is affected; as arm-level when 50% or more of the chromosome arm is affected; and as focal when affecting less than 50% of the chromosome arm. Percentages for relative lengths are customizable.' Broad = chromosomal + arm-level; the Introduction restates it as 'broad CNAs, which are defined as whole-chromosome and chromosomal arm-level alterations'. Amplitude weights A (Table 1): log2 >= 1 high-level gain (>=4 copies) A=3; >= 0.58 medium gain ([3-4) copies) A=2; >= 0.2 low gain ([2.3-3] copies) A=1; <= -0.2 low loss ((1-1.7] copies) A=1; <= -1 medium loss ((0.6-1] copies) A=2; <= -1.74 high loss (<=0.6 copies) A=3; and [-0.2, 0.2] with BAF >= 0.25 is copy-neutral loss-of-heterozygosity at A=2. Focal coverage punctuation L (Table 2): <=5% arm coverage L=1; >5-15% L=2; >15-30% L=3; >30% L=4. BCS(x) = sum_{i=1}^{N} A_i over the N broad events in sample x - A SINGLE SCALAR PER SAMPLE, a weighted COUNT of altered arms and chromosomes, NOT a per-arm vector and NOT a mean absolute log2. FCS(x) = sum A_i * L_i over focal events. GCS(x) = normBCS(x) + normFCS(x), each z-scored across samples. Observed pan-cancer ranges on 10,635 samples: BCS 0-44, FCS 5-2466, GCS -1.93 to 12.60; Spearman correlation of each score with the corresponding fraction of altered genome: BCS 0.957, FCS 0.938, GCS 0.963; inter-score Spearman BCS-FCS 0.59, BCS-GCS 0.90, FCS-GCS 0.85. COLON MOLECULAR SUBTYPE - THE BURDEN-ALONE NUMBER DOES NOT EXIST. There is NO accuracy, NO AUC and no metric of any kind for a model built on BROAD SCORES ALONE predicting CMS, and no broad-plus-focal CMS model either. BCS against CMS is reported only as a significance test: 'While BCS established significant differences between CMS paired comparisons (p<=0.0001, Student's t-test), FCS poorly discerned CMS1 from three and CMS2 from 4', followed by 'we reasoned that broad CNAs rather than focal were able to better discriminate between different CMS groups.' The only CMS CLASSIFIER uses a PER-ARM PATTERN rather than the burden scalar: 'applying machine learning-based prediction models to classify samples by the most discriminative descriptive regions across CMS groups (i.e. 13q, 17 p, 18, and 20q), CNApp reached 55% of accuracy to correctly predict CMS. In fact, the occurrence of these genomic alterations was able to differentiate CMS2 from CMS4 with an accuracy of 70%, and CMS1 from CMS3 with a 72.3% accuracy. As expected, this set of genomic alterations distinguished CMS1 from CMS2 samples with an accuracy of 95%.' The split protocol is NR in that CMS paragraph itself - the 50-permutation 75/25 randomForest protocol is the Classifier model's documented default and is stated explicitly only for the MSI analysis. MICROSATELLITE INSTABILITY, the one place a burden scalar is scored as a classifier: 'Our results showed an average BCS of 1.51 +/- 2.11 and 10.25 +/- 5.92 for MSI (N = 72) and MSS (N = 225) tumors, respectively'; 'Global accuracy in average for the 50-permutation in the RandomForest model was 82.2%'; 'further analysis by ROC curve implementation between MSI and MSS groups with BCS values as classifier proxy resulted in an AUC of 0.917' - a BINARY AUC, MSI vs MSS, colon, from the single BCS scalar. Threshold selection: the intersection between predicted MSI and MSS groups falls at BCS = 4.75, while 'the intersection between sensitivity and specificity from ROC analysis resulted in a BCS value of 3.5' - though the Figure 4-figure supplement 1E legend instead says 'showing the intersection value of 3.75 (green vertical line)', an internal inconsistency in the published paper; a threshold of BCS = 4 was adopted. Independent validation (Berg et al. 2019, n=147): 'we obtained a global accuracy of 81%, which is similar to the accuracy obtained in the COAD dataset (82.2%)'. PAN-CANCER TISSUE-OF-ORIGIN - NO CLASSIFIER METRIC EXISTS: the abstract's claim that CNAs classify cancer types by tissue of origin is backed only by UNSUPERVISED HIERARCHICAL CLUSTERING of mean arm-region profiles over 20 of 33 cancer types and 8,653 samples ('correlation values resulting from Pearson's test hierarchically clustered according to the tissue-of-origin from the tumor'), with no accuracy, AUC or confusion matrix. BREAST, in full: 'breast cancer (BRCA) samples displayed high FCS values (median FCS value of 150), while BCS values were only intermediate (median BCS value of 7).'
rows.external_validation: YES for the MSI threshold only: 'In order to validate that a BCS value of 4 was able to predict microsatellite status, we used a completely independent CRC cohort (Berg et al., 2019). The validation dataset consisted of segmented data from 147 samples with known microsatellite status and CMS annotation (MSI, N = 28; MSS, N = 119; CMS1, N = 27; CMS2, N = 61; CMS3, N = 29; CMS4, N = 30). We then ran CNApp to obtain BCS values for each sample and applied our BCS of 4 as the threshold to re-classify samples ... By doing so, we obtained a global accuracy of 81%.' The threshold itself was SELECTED on the COAD cohort and only APPLIED to the validation cohort, which is a clean protocol. The CMS classification result (55%) has NO external validation. The authors state the limitation themselves: 'the output from the Classifier model would need to be further validated using alternative prediction algorithms and/or independent datasets'.
rows.code: Tool hosted at https://tools.idibaps.org/CNApp/; source at GitHub (Franch-Exposito, 2020), archived at https://github.com/elifesciences-publications/CNApp. Built with Shiny 1.1.0 and R 3.4.2.
rows.caveats: Retrieved open access from the Europe PMC REST fullTextXML endpoint for PMC7010409 (HTTP 200); note that an initial guess of PMC7028453 returned HTTP 404, so the PMCID must be resolved via the DOI rather than guessed. THE HEADLINE CAVEAT: this paper does NOT contain a metric for 'broad scores alone predicting a molecular subtype'. For CMS the burden score is only shown to differ significantly between groups by t-test, and the only CMS classifier is built on four ARM REGIONS (13q, 17p, 18, 20q) - a pattern, not a burden. The one place a burden scalar is scored as a classifier is the BINARY MSI endpoint (AUC 0.917, accuracy 82.2%), which is a different disease and a two-class problem. OTHER CAVEATS: the 55% CMS accuracy is a 4-class accuracy against a 36% majority class (CMS2 112/309), so it is weak, and no balanced accuracy or per-class recall is given; the sensitivity/specificity intersection is stated inconsistently (body 3.5, figure legend 3.75); the randomForest Classifier model is described by the authors themselves as a screening aid rather than a validated predictor; and ZERO occurrences of 'PAM50', 'luminal' or 'intrinsic subtype' appear in the entire full text (case-insensitive 'breast' = 1 hit and 'BRCA' = 1 hit, i.e. that single sentence is the whole breast content), so nothing here is a breast subtype result. Note for anyone re-checking: the 0.917 AUC and the 82.2% accuracy appear twice in the Europe PMC XML, once in the Results and once in the appended eLife decision letter / author response, with identical values. Refereed. HOW TO USE IT: context only, for the aneuploidy-burden control rather than for any headline number, and its figures must never be tabulated beside any number here - wrong disease (colorectal), wrong endpoint (CMS and MSI, not PAM50), and for the multiclass endpoint no burden-alone metric exists at all. What it is genuinely good for: (1) it supplies a PUBLISHED, PEER-REVIEWED FORMAL DEFINITION of an arm-scale burden scalar - BCS as the sum of amplitude weights over broad (>=50% of a chromosome arm) events - which is a different statistic from mean_abs_log2 and from frac_altered, so citing it lets the config-key-not-unwritten-assumption choice be positioned against prior art rather than invented; (2) it establishes the burden-versus-pattern distinction as a published concern and shows the two behave differently (BCS-FCS Spearman only 0.59 pan-cancer); (3) it shows a burden scalar CAN carry real signal on a binary endpoint (MSI vs MSS, AUC 0.917) while an arm PATTERN is what gets used when the endpoint is 4-class (CMS, 55% from four arms), which is directionally the same story as one scalar reaching 0.685 while 39 arms reach 0.866-0.888; and (4) most importantly, after this reading the burden-versus-pattern control here still has NO direct counterpart in the literature - no paper found reports how well a scalar aneuploidy measure alone discriminates PAM50 classes - so that absence should be stated as a positive contribution, with CNApp cited as the nearest analogue rather than as a precedent.

rows.title: UniCat: Crafting a Stronger Fusion Baseline for Multimodal Re-Identification
rows.authors: Jennifer Crawford, Haoli Yin, Luke McDermott, Daniel Cummings (Modern Intelligence)
rows.venue: arXiv:2310.18812v1 [cs.CV], submitted 28 Oct 2023 (v1 is the only version). WORKSHOP-REFEREED AT BEST: the arXiv Comments field reads 'Accepted NeurIPS 2023 UniReps, 9 pages, 4 tables' - a NeurIPS workshop, not the main track - while the PDF's own page-1 footer still reads 'Preprint. Under review.', and the arXiv record carries no journal_ref.
rows.doi: NR as a publisher DOI; the arXiv abs page lists https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2310.18812 and the arXiv record's own doi field is empty.
rows.modalities: Visible-spectrum RGB, near-infrared (NIR) and thermal-infrared (TIR) images. NOT a medical or biological paper.
rows.datasets: RGBNT100 (multimodal vehicle ReID, RGB+NIR+TIR, 'for 100 vehicles'); RGBN300 (RGB+NIR pairs, 'for 300 vehicles'); RGBNT201 (multimodal person ReID, RGB+NIR+TIR triples, 'for 201 different individuals'); Market1501 (unimodal person ReID, used only in the Appendix C ensemble experiment) - Market1501's identity count is NOT stated in the paper text and is NR here rather than inferred from the dataset name.
rows.endpoint: Object and person re-identification retrieval - matching instances of the same object across sensors and time, with identities seen at training not overlapping those at inference. NOT a classification endpoint. CLASS COUNT: NR and not applicable (open-set retrieval, not classification into a fixed class set). PREDICTION UNIT: per-image / per-identity retrieval; not applicable to the patch/slide/case taxonomy. LABEL BASIS: not applicable - object identity labels, no biological labels.
rows.wsi_pipeline: N/A - no pathology. Backbones are ResNet-50 and ViT-B; images are resized to 128x256 (RGBNT100/RGBN300) or 256x128 (RGBNT201).
rows.fusion_method: Three strategies differing ONLY in whether the loss is global or local. Formalisation verbatim: 'for each modality we train an unshared backbone, f_i that produces a modality-specific embedding, z_i. These modality-specific embeddings can then be combined into a multimodal representation: z_fuse = Theta(z_1, z_2, ...z_M) where Theta is the chosen fusion operator.' Fusion-avg and Fusion-concat 'use a global loss function that operates on the fused multimodal representation, z_fuse: L_fusion = L(z_fuse, y_fuse). In this case, the back-propagated gradients for each modality are entangled'. UniCat instead trains 'each modality encoder independently with their own local loss function: L_post = sum_i L(z_i, y_i)... Here, note that each modality's loss is fully disentangled from the others. In this case, fusion occurs only at inference when we concatenate the modality-specific embeddings into the final multimodal representation, z_fuse.' Loss is a soft-margin triplet loss with hard mining plus cross-entropy, lambda = 1, BNNeck before CE. CRITICAL DISANALOGY: FUSION-AVG AVERAGES EMBEDDINGS (latent representations), NOT OUTPUT PROBABILITIES - the formalisation operates on z_i, and the Results confirm 'Because the multimodal embeddings in all fusion cases are simply poolings of unimodal embeddings, multimodal ReID performance here is closely tied to the corresponding unimodal ReID performance'. An equal-weight probability mean never touches representations at all, so UniCat's Fusion-avg must NOT be described as a probability average.
rows.metrics: All metrics are retrieval mAP and Rank-1 from the cumulative match curve, on each dataset's fixed train/test identity split, 'calculated by averaging performance across four random seeds' (the typo 'calcluated' is in the source caption); the +/- values are across those four seeds. There is no cross-validation and no external cohort. TABLE 1, ViT-B rows (mAP | Rank-1): RGBNT100 - Fusion-avg 76.1 +/- 0.3 | 90.1 +/- 0.9; Fusion-concat 75.9 +/- 0.7 | 92.3 +/- 0.4; UniCat 81.3 +/- 0.9 | 97.5 +/- 0.3. RGBN300 - Fusion-avg 78.1 +/- 0.1 | 91.4 +/- 0.4; Fusion-concat 77.4 +/- 0.3 | 91.8 +/- 0.3; UniCat 80.2 +/- 0.2 | 92.9 +/- 0.4. RGBNT201 - Fusion-avg 56.1 +/- 2.2 | 54.9 +/- 1.8; Fusion-concat 61.7 +/- 2.1 | 60.6 +/- 1.2; UniCat 57.6 +/- 2.0 | 58.0 +/- 1.8. TABLE 1, ResNet-50 rows: RGBNT100 - 75.3 +/- 0.6 | 92.2 +/- 0.9; 75.1 +/- 0.9 | 92.7 +/- 0.6; 79.4 +/- 0.5 | 94.9 +/- 0.8. RGBN300 - 74.9 +/- 0.5 | 91.2 +/- 0.6; 74.7 +/- 0.4 | 91.3 +/- 0.2; 76.7 +/- 0.4 | 92.3 +/- 0.4. RGBNT201 - 57.6 +/- 2.9 | 61.0 +/- 3.0; 63.0 +/- 1.9 | 66.7 +/- 3.1; 38.1 +/- 1.3 | 33.6 +/- 1.7. SOTA baselines in the same table: PFNET 68.1/94.1 and 31.8/54.6; IEEE 61.3/87.8 and 46.42/47.13; HAMNet 64.1/84.7, 61.9/84.0, 27.68/26.32; CCNet 77.2/96.3; PHT 79.9/92.7 and 79.3/93.7. NOTE THE CONTRARY RESULT: on RGBNT201 the JOINTLY TRAINED Fusion-concat WINS on both backbones (63.0 vs UniCat 38.1 on ResNet-50; 61.7 vs 57.6 on ViT-B), which the authors explain as modality laziness protecting a weak, noisy modality - 'We can consider this modality a weak-link since when trained in isolation (UniCat) its performance is notably lower than RGB/TIR. As multimodal ReID is most affected by the weakest-link, we deduce that the performance gains of NIR in the case of Fusion-concat outweighed the performance drops in RGB/TIR.' APPENDIX C TABLE 4, the same-modality two-backbone ensemble, ViT-B (mAP | Rank-1) - the control a fusion ladder typically lacks: RGBNT100-RGB Fusion avg 57.7 | 79.1; Fusion-concat 58.4 | 81.0; UniCat 60.4 | 84.4. RGBNT100-NIR 48.6 | 67.7; 48.9 | 70.0; 50.7 | 72.9. RGBNT100-TIR 48.6 | 76.9; 47.4 | 80.8; 49.7 | 81.1. Market1501 87.6 | 94.9; 87.9 | 94.8; 89.1 | 95.4. No +/- values are given in Table 4 - the four-seed averaging is stated for Table 1 only, so Table 4's repeat protocol is NR. THE VERBATIM CLAIM: 'However, what is notable is that in all unimodal tasks, training the ensemble using a global loss (Fusion-avg/concat) resulted in a lower performance than would otherwise have been obtained if each member were trained independently (UniCat). This underscores the fundamental nature by which modality laziness operates and how the phenomenon should be considered even when training with balanced modalities.' TABLES 2 and 3 show the mechanism: on RGBNT100 with ViT-B, UniCat's individual encoders reach RGB 58.4 +/- 0.83, NIR 51.4 +/- 0.8, TIR 46.1 +/- 2.5 mAP against Fusion-avg's 51.7 +/- 0.8, 41.8 +/- 0.6 and 31.0 +/- 0.9 - joint training degrades each constituent encoder. Appendix D confirms the same degradation on the TRAINING set, which rules out overfitting as the explanation, quoted in full because the truncated version drops a qualifier: 'Mirroring the test behavior, we see that the unimodal mAP for the train set was inhibited for Fusion-avg and Fusion-concat compared to UniCat. Thus, contrary to the hypothesis of [14], the performance decline that we observed when training with fusion (Table 1) can be primarily linked to modality laziness, and it is actually UniCat that appears to be more at risk for overfitting.'
rows.external_validation: None in the sense this survey means. Each dataset has its own disjoint-identity train/test split; there is no transfer to a second corpus and no cross-dataset evaluation. Market1501 in Appendix C is a separate experiment, not a validation of the RGBNT100 result.
rows.code: NR - no code or repository link appears in the paper text.
rows.caveats: UNREFEREED beyond NeurIPS 2023 UniReps workshop review; the PDF itself still says 'Preprint. Under review.' and the arXiv record carries no journal_ref. DOMAIN: multimodal person and vehicle re-identification - this is precedent for a PHENOMENON and for a CONTROL DESIGN, never for a number, since mAP and Rank-1 are retrieval metrics with no relationship to macro AUROC. TWO SPECIFIC LIMITS ON HOW FAR IT TRANSFERS: (1) their Fusion-avg averages EMBEDDINGS, not output probabilities, so the operator that loses in their paper is closer to the concat/gated arms here than to an untrained probability mean, and an untrained-average baseline has no counterpart in their design; (2) their result REVERSES on RGBNT201, where jointly trained Fusion-concat beats UniCat on both backbones, and the authors' own framing is a double-edged sword in which modality laziness protects noisy weak modalities - any citation that omits the RGBNT201 reversal is selective. Table 4 also reports no seed variance and no significance test, so the roughly 2-3 mAP gaps it rests on are unquantified. Market1501's identity count is NR. HOW TO USE IT: context only, and specifically context for the fusion-operator MECHANISM and for the stated OPEN CONFOUND, never for any number. THE SINGLE MOST VALUABLE FACT, and it bears directly on that confound: in Appendix C the two ensemble members DO share an initialisation - 'We choose ViT-B as our model backbone and use ImageNet pre-trained weights. The classifiers and bottlenecks are randomly instantiated via [5], so that we may fully expect the backbones to have unique final solutions', with Appendix B confirming the same for the main Table 1 runs. So both backbones start from the SAME ImageNet checkpoint, with diversity coming only from randomly initialised classifier and bottleneck heads and from data ordering - and independent training STILL beats joint training on all four same-modality tasks (RGB 60.4 vs 58.4/57.7; NIR 50.7 vs 48.9/48.6; TIR 49.7 vs 48.6/47.4; Market1501 89.1 vs 87.9/87.6). That is precisely the discriminating experiment a warm-started fusion ladder is missing: it holds shared initialisation FIXED and varies only global-versus-local loss, and the diversity collapse still appears. It is therefore published support for reading phi = 0.656 among jointly trained operators against 0.193 between independent unimodal arms as a JOINT-TRAINING effect rather than a shared-warm-start effect - while remaining, in a different domain, evidence about the mechanism and not proof about this data. It also independently motivates running a no-warm-start arm: UniCat shows the effect survives shared initialisation, not that shared initialisation contributes nothing. Cite it for the phenomenon, for 'modality laziness' as the named mechanism (Du et al. 2023; Peng et al. 2022 for gradient entanglement), for the same-modality ensemble control and its shared-initialisation detail, and for the authors' own recommendation - 'We encourage researchers in this field to validate simple post-training fusion baselines like UniCat first in their setting, before pursuing more complex fusion strategies' - always alongside the RGBNT201 reversal.
